sentences.zh: 王沈

translations.literal: Wang Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Wang Shen.

sentences.zh: 王沈，字處道，太原晉陽人也。

translations.literal: Wang Shen, courtesy name Chudao, was a man of Jinyang in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen, whose courtesy name was Chudao, came from Jinyang in Taiyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖柔，漢匈奴中郎將。

translations.literal: His grandfather Rou had been Colonel of the Xiongnu in the Han.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wang Rou had served the Han as Colonel of the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 父機，魏東郡太守。

translations.literal: His father Ji had been Administrator of Dong commandery in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Ji had been Wei’s administrator of Dong commandery.

sentences.zh: 沈少孤，養于從叔司空昶，事昶如父。

translations.literal: Shen in his youth was orphaned; he was raised by his paternal cousin, Minister of Works Chang, and served Chang as a father.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen lost his parents while still young and was brought up by his cousin, the Minister of Works Wang Chang, whom he honored as he would a father.

sentences.zh: 奉繼母寡嫂以孝義稱。

translations.literal: He served his stepmother and widowed sister-in-law and was praised for filial piety and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He cared devotedly for his stepmother and his widowed sister-in-law and won a reputation for filial duty and decency.

sentences.zh: 好書，善屬文。

translations.literal: He loved books and was good at composing texts.
translations.idiomatic: He was a devoted reader and a skilled writer.

sentences.zh: 大將軍曹爽辟為掾，累遷中書門下侍郎。

translations.literal: Grand General Cao Shuang summoned him as a clerk; he was promoted in stages to Gentleman of the Palace Gate under the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The grand general Cao Shuang appointed him to his staff, and he rose step by step to the post of gentleman attendant at the palace gate under the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及爽誅，以故吏免。

translations.literal: When Shuang was executed, because he was a former subordinate he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Shuang was put to death, Wang Shen was removed from office as one of his former retainers.

sentences.zh: 後起為治書侍御史，轉秘書監。

translations.literal: Later he was raised up as Palace Assistant Clerk and transferred to Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recalled as assistant clerk for judicial documents, then promoted to director of the imperial library.

sentences.zh: 正元中，遷散騎常侍、侍中，典著作。

translations.literal: In the Zhengyuan years he was promoted to Regular Cavalier Attendant and Palace Attendant and supervised composition of texts.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengyuan era he rose to regular cavalier attendant and palace attendant and took charge of historiographical compilation.

sentences.zh: 與荀顗、阮籍共撰《魏書》，多為時諱，未若陳壽之實錄也。

translations.literal: Together with Xun Yi and Ruan Ji he compiled the *Book of Wei*; it contained many taboos for the times and did not match Chen Shou’s true record.
translations.idiomatic: With Xun Yi and Ruan Ji he co-authored the *Book of Wei*, but it bowed so often to contemporary sensitivities that it fell short of Chen Shou’s straightforward annals.

sentences.zh: 時魏高貴鄉公好學有文才，引沈及裴秀數於東堂講宴屬文，號沈為文籍先生，秀為儒林丈人。

translations.literal: At that time Wei’s Duke of Gaoguixiang loved learning and had literary talent; he brought in Shen and Pei Xiu repeatedly to the Eastern Hall to lecture, feast, and compose texts, calling Shen Master of Documents and Xiu Elder of the Confucian Grove.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler, the Duke of Gaoguixiang, was studious and literary; he repeatedly summoned Wang Shen and Pei Xiu to the Eastern Hall for discourses, banquets, and composition, dubbing Shen “Master of the Archives” and Xiu “Patriarch of the Confucian scholars.”

sentences.zh: 及高貴鄉公將攻文帝，召沈及王業告之，沈、業馳白帝，以功封安平侯，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Gaoguixiang was about to attack Emperor Wen, he summoned Shen and Wang Ye and informed them; Shen and Ye galloped to report to the emperor, and for merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Anping with two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Gaoguixiang prepared to move against Sima Zhao, he called in Wang Shen and Wang Ye; the two men rode at once to warn Sima Zhao. For that service Wang Shen was made marquis of Anping with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 沈既不忠於主，甚為眾論所非。

translations.literal: Shen was not loyal to his lord and was greatly condemned in public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had betrayed his sovereign, Wang Shen was roundly condemned in court and country.

sentences.zh: 尋遷尚書，出監豫州諸軍事、奮武將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Minister and went out to supervise military affairs of Yu Province, as General Who Inspires Might and Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon advanced to minister, then sent out to oversee the armies of Yu province as General Who Inspires Might and provincial inspector.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，乃下教曰：「自古賢聖，樂聞誹謗之言，聽輿人之論，芻蕘有可錄之事，負薪有廊廟之語故也。

translations.literal: When he reached his post he issued an instruction saying, ‘From antiquity the worthy and sage have delighted to hear words of blame, listened to the discussions of cart men, because in fodder cutters there are matters worth recording and in firewood bearers there are words fit for the hall of state.’
translations.idiomatic: On arriving at his command he promulgated an edict: ‘Since ancient times, the wise have welcomed blunt criticism and heeded what common people say—grass-cutters may offer something worth recording, and wood-gatherers may speak to the needs of the state.’

sentences.zh: 自至鎮日，未聞逆耳之言，豈未明虛心，故令言者有疑。

translations.literal: From the day I reached this post I have not heard ear-offending words; is it because I have not made clear my emptying of mind, and therefore those who would speak have doubts?’
translations.idiomatic: ‘Since I took up this post I have heard no unwelcome truths; perhaps I have failed to show that I truly wish to listen, and so would-be advisers hold back.’

sentences.zh: 其宣下屬城及士庶，若能舉遺逸于林藪，黜奸佞于州國，陳長吏之可否，說百姓之所患，興利除害，損益昭然者，給穀五百斛。

translations.literal: Let it be proclaimed to subordinate cities and to gentry and commoners: if one can recommend the hidden and reclusive in woods and marshes, dismiss the treacherous and sycophantic in the province and state, state whether senior officials are fit or not, relate what the hundred surnames suffer, promote benefit and remove harm, and gain and loss are clear, give five hundred hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: ‘Publish this to every county seat and to scholars and commoners alike: anyone who can bring forward recluses from the wilds, expose villains in office, judge local magistrates fairly, voice the people’s grievances, or propose clear measures to help the region and curb abuse shall receive five hundred hu of grain.’

sentences.zh: 若達一至之言，說刺史得失，朝政寬猛，令剛柔得適者，給穀千斛。

translations.literal: If one articulates a single utmost word, speaks of the inspector’s gains and losses, court governance lenient or harsh, causing hardness and softness to obtain what is fitting, give one thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: ‘If someone offers a truly penetrating judgment—on my own performance as inspector, or on whether central policy strikes the right balance between severity and leniency—the reward shall be one thousand hu of grain.’

sentences.zh: 謂餘不信，明如皎日。

translations.literal: If you say I am not trustworthy, it is bright as the bright sun.’
translations.idiomatic: ‘As for my sincerity, let the bright sun be witness.’

sentences.zh: 」主簿陳廞、褚䂮曰：「奉省教旨，伏用感歎。

translations.literal: ’ The chief clerk Chen Xin and Chu Lüe said, ‘We have received and examined the instruction’s intent and prostrate ourselves, moved to sigh.
translations.idiomatic: ’ His chief clerks Chen Xin and Chu Lüe replied, ‘We have read your instruction and are deeply moved.’

sentences.zh: 勞謙日昃，思聞苦言。

translations.literal: Laboring in modesty till the sun slants, you desire to hear bitter words.
translations.idiomatic: ‘You weary yourself with humble diligence and long to hear plain, unwelcome counsel.’

sentences.zh: 愚謂上之所好，下無不應。

translations.literal: We foolishly say: what those above love, those below none do not respond to.
translations.idiomatic: ‘We would observe that subjects always take their cue from what their superiors favor.’

sentences.zh: 而近未有極諫之辭，遠無傳言之箴者，誠得失之事將未有也。

translations.literal: Yet nearby there are no words of utmost remonstrance, afar none who transmit admonitions; truly matters of gain and loss perhaps have not yet existed.
translations.idiomatic: ‘Yet we see no blunt remonstrance close at hand and no far-reaching warnings from afar—perhaps there truly are no issues of right and wrong to report.’

sentences.zh: 今使教命班下，示以賞勸，將恐拘介之士，或憚賞而不言；

translations.literal: Now if we cause the instruction to be promulgated below and show them reward and encouragement, we fear that stiff and principled gentlemen may perhaps fear the reward and not speak;
translations.idiomatic: ‘If we now publish this offer of grain, scrupulous men may keep silent for fear of seeming to seek a prize.’

sentences.zh: 貪賕之人，將慕利而妄舉。

translations.literal: greedy bribe-taking men will admire profit and recklessly bring charges.
translations.idiomatic: ‘While the corrupt will invent accusations to chase the reward.’

sentences.zh: 苟不合宜，賞不虛行，則遠聽者未知當否之所在，徒見言之不用，謂設有而不行。

translations.literal: If it is not fitting and reward is not given emptily, then those who listen from afar will not know where right and wrong lie; they will merely see that words are not used and say it is established but not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: ‘If advice is poor and no bounty is paid without cause, onlookers will still not grasp what was amiss; they will only see counsel spurned and conclude the measure was proclaimed but never implemented.’

sentences.zh: 愚以告下之事，可小須後。」

translations.literal: We foolishly think the matter of proclaiming below may slightly wait until later.’
translations.idiomatic: ‘We therefore ask that the promulgation of this policy be deferred a little.’

sentences.zh: 沈又教曰：「夫德薄而位厚，功輕而祿重，貪夫之所徇，高士之所不處也。

translations.literal: Shen again instructed saying, ‘Now virtue thin and position thick, merit light and salary heavy—what the greedy man pursues, the lofty gentleman does not abide in.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen issued another instruction: ‘High office with meager virtue, and rich stipends for slight achievement—such things attract the grasping but repel the principled.’

sentences.zh: 若陳至言于刺史，興益於本州，達幽隱之賢，去祝鮀之佞，立德於上，受分於下，斯乃君子之操，何不言之有！

translations.literal: If one presents utmost words to the inspector, raises benefit in this province, brings forth the hidden worthy, removes Zhu Tuo’s sycophancy, establishes virtue above and receives allotment below—this then is the conduct of the gentleman; how could there be not speaking!’
translations.idiomatic: ‘Speak the hard truth to your inspector, strengthen this province, lift up recluses of talent, drive out flatterers like Zhu Tuo, let superiors win moral authority and subordinates earn their due—that is how gentlemen behave; who could then refuse to speak up?’

sentences.zh: 直言至理，忠也。

translations.literal: Straight words and utmost principle—that is loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: ‘Plain speech that hits the mark is loyalty.’

sentences.zh: 惠加一州，仁也。

translations.literal: Favor extending to one province—that is benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: ‘A policy that blesses the whole province is benevolence.’

sentences.zh: 功成辭賞，廉也。

translations.literal: Merit accomplished and declining reward—that is integrity.
translations.idiomatic: ‘To achieve much yet decline reward is integrity.’

sentences.zh: 兼斯而行，仁智之事，何故懷其道而迷其國哉！

translations.literal: Combining these and practicing them are matters of benevolence and wisdom; why harbor its way and confuse the state!’
translations.idiomatic: ‘Practice all of this and you unite humanity and wisdom—why clutch your principles in private and leave the realm adrift?’

sentences.zh: 」褚䂮復白曰：「堯、舜、周公所以能致忠諫者，以其款誠之心著也。

translations.literal: ’ Chu Lüe again reported saying, ‘The reason Yao, Shun, and the Duke of Zhou could bring forth loyal remonstrance was that their sincere and earnest hearts were manifest.
translations.idiomatic: ’ Chu Lüe replied again: ‘Yao, Shun, and the Duke of Zhou won honest counsel because their own sincerity was unmistakable.’

sentences.zh: 冰炭不言，而冷熱之質自明者，以其有實也。

translations.literal: Ice and charcoal do not speak, yet the substance of cold and heat is self-evident because they have reality.
translations.idiomatic: ‘Ice and charcoal need not speak: their cold and heat are obvious because they are real.’

sentences.zh: 若好忠直，如冰炭之自然，則諤諤之臣，將濟濟而盈庭；

translations.literal: If one loves loyalty and uprightness like ice and charcoal’s naturalness, then outspoken ministers will be numerous and fill the court;
translations.idiomatic: ‘If you truly love blunt integrity as naturally as ice is cold and fire hot, forthright officials will throng your hall.’

sentences.zh: 逆耳之言，不求而自至。

translations.literal: ear-offending words, not sought, arrive of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: ‘Unwelcome truths will come unbidden.’

sentences.zh: 若德不足以配唐虞，明不足以並周公，實不可以同冰炭，雖懸重賞，忠諫之言未可致也。

translations.literal: If virtue is insufficient to match Tang and Yu, clarity insufficient to stand beside the Duke of Zhou, substance cannot be the same as ice and charcoal; though heavy rewards are hung, words of loyal remonstrance cannot be brought forth.
translations.idiomatic: ‘But if one’s virtue cannot rival the sage-kings of antiquity nor one’s discernment match the Duke of Zhou—if one lacks that elemental clarity—then no heap of grain will buy loyal criticism.’

sentences.zh: 昔魏絳由和戎之功，蒙女樂之賜，管仲有興齊之勳，而加上卿之禮，功勳明著，然後賞勸隨之。

translations.literal: Formerly Wei Jiang because of merit in harmonizing the Rong received the gift of female musicians; Guan Zhong had merit in raising Qi and received the rites of a senior minister; merit and achievement were clear and manifest, and afterward reward and encouragement followed.
translations.idiomatic: ‘In old days Wei Jiang was given musicians after pacifying the Rong; Guan Zhong was honored as chief minister after restoring Qi—rewards followed proven achievement.’

sentences.zh: 未聞張重賞以待諫臣，懸穀帛以求盡言也。

translations.literal: I have not heard of spreading heavy reward to await remonstrating ministers, hanging grain and silk to seek exhaustive words.’
translations.idiomatic: ‘I have never heard of posting grain and silk to purchase advice before any deed is done.’

sentences.zh: 」沈無以奪之，遂從䂮議。

translations.literal: ’ Shen had nothing with which to overrule him and followed Lüe’s proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen could not refute him and accepted Chu Lüe’s recommendation.

sentences.zh: 沈探尋善政，案賈逵以來法制禁令，諸所施行，擇善者而從之。

translations.literal: Shen investigated good governance, examined laws, systems, and prohibitions since Jia Kui, and among what had been implemented selected the good and followed them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen studied effective administration, reviewed statutes and bans in force since Jia Kui’s time, and adopted the best of what earlier regimes had tried.

sentences.zh: 又教曰：「後生不聞先王之教，而望政道日興，不可得也。

translations.literal: He also instructed saying, ‘The later born do not hear the former kings’ teaching, yet hope governance daily rises—it cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: He further instructed: ‘If the young never hear the teaching of the ancient kings, you cannot expect government to improve day by day.’

sentences.zh: 文武並用，長久之道也。

translations.literal: Civil and military together used is the way of length and endurance.
translations.idiomatic: ‘Civil and military arts must work together—that is how a state endures.’

sentences.zh: 俗化陵遲，不可不革。

translations.literal: Custom and transformation decline; it cannot be not reformed.
translations.idiomatic: ‘Popular morals are sliding; reform is unavoidable.’

sentences.zh: 革俗之要，實在敦學。

translations.literal: The essential of reforming custom lies truly in promoting learning.
translations.idiomatic: ‘The heart of moral renewal is serious education.’

sentences.zh: 昔原伯魯不悅學，閔馬父知其必亡。

translations.literal: Formerly Yuan Bolu did not delight in learning; Min Mafu knew he would surely perish.
translations.idiomatic: ‘When Yuan Bolu of old disdained study, Min Mafu foretold his ruin.’

sentences.zh: 將吏子弟，優閑家門，若不教之，必致遊戲，傷毀風俗矣。

translations.literal: Sons and younger brothers of generals and clerks, leisurely at home gates—if we do not teach them, they will surely lead to wandering play and wound and destroy custom.’
translations.idiomatic: ‘Officers’ sons idle at home; left untaught they turn to dissipation and poison local custom.’

sentences.zh: 」於是九郡之士，咸悅道教，移風易俗。

translations.literal: ’ Thereupon gentlemen of the nine commanderies all delighted in the way’s teaching and shifted wind and changed custom.
translations.idiomatic: After that, educated men across the nine commanderies embraced his educational policy, and customs began to change for the better.

sentences.zh: 遷征虜將軍、持節、都督江北諸軍事。

translations.literal: He was promoted General Who Conquers Captives, credential bearer, and area commander of all military affairs north of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Conquers Captives, given the imperial baton, and made area commander of all forces north of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 五等初建，封博陵侯，班在次國。

translations.literal: When the five ranks were first established, he was enfeoffed Marquis of Boling, ranked among the secondary states.
translations.idiomatic: When the five grades of nobility were first instituted, he became marquis of Boling, listed among the second-tier fiefs.

sentences.zh: 平蜀之役，吳人大出，聲為救蜀，振盪邊境，沈鎮禦有方，寇聞而退。

translations.literal: In the campaign to pacify Shu, Wu men came out in great force, declaring they would rescue Shu, shaking the border; Shen defended with method, and the raiders heard and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: During the conquest of Shu, Wu sent a large force toward the frontier on the pretext of aiding Shu; Wang Shen organized the defense so skillfully that the enemy withdrew without a fight.

sentences.zh: 轉鎮南將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Guards the South.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as General Who Guards the South.

sentences.zh: 武帝即王位，拜御史大夫，守尚書令，加給事中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu assumed the king’s position, he was appointed Grandee Secretary, acting Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and added Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yan took the title of king, Wang Shen was named grandee secretary, acting director of the secretariat, with additional duty as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 沈以才望，顯名當世，是以創業之事，羊祜、荀勖、裴秀、賈充等，皆與沈諮謀焉。

translations.literal: Shen by talent and reputation had a clear name in the age; therefore in matters of founding enterprise Yang Hu, Xun Xu, Pei Xiu, Jia Chong, and others all consulted and planned with Shen.
translations.idiomatic: His talent and prestige made him a leading figure of the day, so Yang Hu, Xun Xu, Pei Xiu, Jia Chong, and others all sought his counsel as the new dynasty took shape.

sentences.zh: 及帝受禪，以佐命之勳，轉驃騎將軍、錄尚書事，加散騎常侍，統城外諸軍事。

translations.literal: When the emperor received the abdication, by merit as assistant to the mandate he was transferred to General of Agile Cavalry, recording Masters of Writing affairs, added Regular Cavalier Attendant, commanding all military affairs outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Yan accepted the Wei abdication, Wang Shen was rewarded for his role in the transition with promotion to General of Agile Cavalry, recorder of the secretariat, concurrent regular cavalier attendant, and command of all troops outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 封博陵郡公，固讓不受，乃進爵為縣公，邑千八百戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed Duke of Boling commandery, firmly declined and did not accept, and then advanced in rank to county duke with one thousand eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered the ducal title for Boling commandery but firmly declined, accepting instead advancement to county duke with a fief of eighteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 帝方欲委以萬機，薨。

translations.literal: The emperor was just about to entrust him with the myriad threads; he died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was on the verge of handing him the full burden of state when Wang Shen died.

sentences.zh: 帝素服舉哀，賜秘器朝服一具、衣一襲、錢三十萬、布百匹、葬田一頃，諡曰元。

translations.literal: The emperor in plain garb raised mourning, bestowed secret burial goods, one set of court dress, one suit of clothes, three hundred thousand cash, one hundred bolts of cloth, one qing of burial land, posthumous name Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore mourning dress for him, granted imperial coffin fittings, a full set of court robes, another suit, three hundred thousand cash, a hundred bolts of cloth, and one qing of burial land, and gave him the posthumous name Yuan (“Primordial”).

sentences.zh: 明年，帝追思沈勳，詔曰：「夫表揚往行，所以崇賢垂訓，慎終紀遠，厚德興教也。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor recalled Shen’s merit and issued an edict saying, ‘Now displaying and raising past conduct is the means to honor the worthy and hand down instruction, be careful at the end and record the distant, thick virtue and raise teaching.’
translations.idiomatic: The following year, remembering Wang Shen’s service, the emperor issued an edict: ‘To honor past conduct is to exalt the worthy, instruct posterity, give the dead their due, and teach generosity.’

sentences.zh: 故散騎常侍、驃騎將軍、博陵元公沈蹈禮居正，執心清粹，經綸墳典，才識通洽。

translations.literal: The former Regular Cavalier Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, Duke Yuan of Boling Shen trod ritual and dwelt in rectitude, held a heart clear and pure, organized the classical tomes, talent and knowledge thorough and comprehensive.
translations.idiomatic: ‘The late Regular Cavalier Attendant and General of Agile Cavalry, Duke Yuan of Boling, walked the path of ritual and integrity, kept a lucid mind, mastered the classics, and united broad talent with sound judgment.’

sentences.zh: 入歷常伯納言之位，出幹監牧方岳之任，內著謀猷，外宣威略。

translations.literal: Entering he passed through Elder of the Palace positions for receiving words; going out he managed supervision and shepherding and regional peak duties; within he showed planning and strategy, without he displayed might and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: ‘At court he held offices that brought counsel to the throne; in the provinces he governed regions and armies; within the capital he framed policy, on the borders he projected authority.’

sentences.zh: 建國設官，首登公輔，兼統中朝，出納大命，實有翼亮佐世之勳。

translations.literal: Establishing the state and setting officials, he first ascended to duke and assistant, concurrently commanded the central court, issued and received the great mandate; truly he had merit as wing and brightness assisting the age.
translations.idiomatic: ‘When the new dynasty was founded he was among the first chief ministers, directed the central government, and conveyed the sovereign’s commands—truly he helped steady the realm.’

sentences.zh: 其贈沈司空公，以寵靈既往，使沒而不朽。

translations.literal: Let Shen be posthumously gifted Minister of Works duke, by favoring the spirit already gone, causing him to die yet not decay.
translations.idiomatic: ‘Posthumously appoint him Minister of Works so that imperial favor may follow him beyond the grave and his name endure.’

sentences.zh: 又前以翼贊之勳，當受郡公之封，而固辭懇至，嘉其讓德，不奪其志。

translations.literal: Moreover earlier because of wing-assist merit he ought to have received commandery duke enfeoffment, but firmly declined with utmost sincerity; we praised his yielding virtue and did not seize his intent.
translations.idiomatic: ‘He had earned a commandery dukedom for aiding the throne yet begged to decline it; we honored his modesty and did not force the higher title on him.’

sentences.zh: 可以郡公官屬送葬。

translations.literal: He may use commandery duke official subordinates to escort the burial.’
translations.idiomatic: ‘Let his funeral be conducted with the escort due a commandery duke.’

sentences.zh: 沈素清儉，不營產業。

translations.literal: Shen was by nature clear and frugal and did not manage estates.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen had always lived plainly and accumulated no property.

sentences.zh: 其使所領兵作屋五十間。

translations.literal: Let him cause the troops he leads to build fifty rooms.’
translations.idiomatic: ‘Order the soldiers under his command to erect fifty rooms’ (for his household).

sentences.zh: 」子浚嗣。

translations.literal: ’ Son Jun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: ’ His son Wang Jun inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 後沈夫人荀氏卒，將合葬，沈棺櫬已毀，更賜東園秘器。

translations.literal: Later Lady Shen nee Xun died; they were about to be jointly buried, but Shen’s coffin shell was already destroyed, and again bestowed Eastern Garden secret goods.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Lady Wang née Xun died and was to be buried with him, his original coffin had decayed, so the court again granted Eastern Garden burial fittings.

sentences.zh: 咸寧中，復追封沈為郡公。

translations.literal: In the Xianning years, again posthumously enfeoffed Shen as commandery duke.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianning he was posthumously raised again to commandery duke.

translations.literal: The text reads '=' (genealogical table marker).
translations.idiomatic: Table notation in the received text (equals sign).

sentences.zh: 子浚

translations.literal: Son Jun.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Jun.

sentences.zh: =浚字彭祖。

translations.literal: = Jun, courtesy name Pengzu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun, courtesy name Pengzu (table line).

sentences.zh: 母趙氏婦，良家女也，貧賤，出入沈家，遂生浚，沈初不齒之。

translations.literal: His mother was a woman of the Zhao clan, a daughter of a good family, poor and low; she went in and out of the Shen household and there bore Jun; Shen at first did not reckon him among his children.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was a poor but respectable young woman surnamed Zhao who frequented the Wang household and bore Wang Jun there; Wang Shen at first refused to acknowledge the boy.

sentences.zh: 年十五，沈薨，無子，親戚共立浚為嗣，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: At age fifteen, Shen died; having no son, relatives together established Jun as heir; he was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jun was fifteen, Wang Shen died without a legitimate son; the clan made him heir, and he was appointed commandant of the imperial son-in-law’s escort.

sentences.zh: 太康初，與諸王侯俱就國。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taikang, together with the various kings and marquises he all went to their states.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taikang he went to his fief along with the other princes and nobles.

sentences.zh: 三年來朝，除員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year he came to court and was appointed Supernumerary Gentleman Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the era he attended court and was named supernumerary gentleman cavalier attendant.

sentences.zh: 元康初，轉員外常侍，遷越騎校尉、右軍將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuankang, he was transferred to Supernumerary Regular Attendant, promoted to Colonel of the Agile Cavalry and General of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Yuankang he moved to supernumerary regular attendant, then rose to colonel of the agile cavalry and general of the right army.

sentences.zh: 出補河內太守，以郡公不得為二千石，轉東中郎將，鎮許昌。

translations.literal: He went out to fill Administrator of Henei; because a commandery duke could not be two thousand shi, he was transferred to General of the Central Army of the East and garrisoned Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as administrator of Henei, but a commandery duke could not legally hold a two-thousand-shi post, so he was reassigned as general of the central army of the east and stationed at Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 及愍懷太子幽于許昌，浚承賈后旨，與黃門孫慮共害太子。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Minhuai was confined at Xuchang, Jun received Empress Jia’s intent and together with Yellow Gate Sun Lü harmed the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: After Crown Prince Minhuai was imprisoned at Xuchang, Wang Jun carried out Empress Jia’s orders and, with the eunuch Sun Lü, murdered the heir.

sentences.zh: 遷寧北將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of Qing province.

sentences.zh: 尋徙寧朔將軍、持節、都督幽州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to General Who Stabilizes the North, credential bearer, area commander of all military affairs of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was reassigned as General Who Stabilizes the Northern Marches, was given the imperial baton, and took overall command of military affairs in You province.

sentences.zh: 于時朝廷昏亂，盜賊蜂起，浚為自安之計，結好夷狄，以女妻鮮卑務勿塵，又以一女妻蘇恕延。

translations.literal: At that time the court was dark and chaotic, bandits and thieves swarmed rising; Jun for a plan of self-security befriended the Yi and Di, giving a daughter in marriage to Xianbei Wuwuchen, and also giving one daughter in marriage to Su Shuyan.
translations.idiomatic: With the court in turmoil and banditry spreading, Wang Jun sought his own safety by allying with non-Chinese peoples: he married a daughter to the Xianbei chief Wuwuchen and another to Su Shuyan.

sentences.zh: 及趙王倫篡位，三王起義兵，浚擁眾挾兩端，遏絕檄書，使其境內士庶不得赴義，成都王穎欲討之而未暇也。

translations.literal: When King Zhao Lun usurped the throne, the three kings raised righteous troops; Jun held the masses and embraced two ends, cut off proclamations, causing gentlemen and commoners within his borders not to be able to join the righteous cause; King of Chengdu Ying wished to attack him but had no leisure.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Lun seized the throne, the three princes rose in revolt; Wang Jun played both sides, blocked their proclamations from his domain, and kept local gentry and commoners from joining the loyalists. Sima Ying of Chengdu wished to punish him but lacked the opportunity.

sentences.zh: 倫誅，進號安北將軍。

translations.literal: When Lun was executed, he advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Lun was put to death, Wang Jun received the higher title General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 及河間王顒、成都王穎興兵內向，害長沙王乂，而浚有不平之心。

translations.literal: When King of Hejian Yong and King of Chengdu Ying raised troops inward and harmed King of Changsha Yi, Jun had an unbalanced heart.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yong of Hejian and Sima Ying of Chengdu marched on the capital and killed Sima Yi of Changsha, Wang Jun nursed a grievance against them.

sentences.zh: 穎表請幽州刺史石堪為右司馬，以右司馬和演代堪，密使演殺浚，並其眾。

translations.literal: Ying memorialized requesting You Province Inspector Shi Kan as Right Major, using Right Major He Yan to replace Kan, secretly ordering Yan to kill Jun and annex his masses.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying petitioned to appoint Shi Kan, inspector of You, as his right major, then replaced Kan with He Yan as right major and secretly instructed He Yan to kill Wang Jun and seize his army.

sentences.zh: 演與烏丸單于審登謀之，於是與浚期遊薊城南清泉水上。

translations.literal: Yan with Wuhuan Chanyu Shen Deng plotted it; thereupon with Jun he made an appointment to roam on the clear spring waters south of Ji city.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan conspired with the Wuhuan chanyu Shen Deng and arranged an outing with Wang Jun to the Clear Spring south of Ji.

sentences.zh: 薊城內西行有二道，演浚各從一道。

translations.literal: Within Ji city going west there were two roads; Yan and Jun each followed one road.
translations.idiomatic: Inside Ji, two roads ran westward; He Yan and Wang Jun each took one.

sentences.zh: 演與浚欲合鹵簿，因而圖之。

translations.literal: Yan and Jun wished to combine halberd escorts and thereby plot him.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan planned to merge his ceremonial escort with Wang Jun’s and strike during the confusion.

sentences.zh: 值天暴雨，兵器沾濕，不果而還。

translations.literal: It happened the heavens poured rain, weapons were damp and wet; it did not succeed and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: A sudden downpour soaked their arms, and the attempt was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 單于由是與其種人謀曰：「演圖殺浚，事垂克而天卒雨，使不得果，是天助浚也。

translations.literal: The chanyu thereby with his kindred plotted saying, ‘Yan plotted to kill Jun; the affair was about to succeed but the heavens finally rained, causing it not to succeed—this is Heaven aiding Jun.’
translations.idiomatic: The chanyu then told his followers, ‘He Yan meant to kill Wang Jun; success was within reach when Heaven sent this rain and foiled him—Heaven favors Wang Jun.’

sentences.zh: 違天不祥，我不可久與演同。

translations.literal: To oppose Heaven is inauspicious; we cannot long be together with Yan.’
translations.idiomatic: ‘To fight Heaven’s intent is ill-omened; we cannot stay allied with He Yan.’

sentences.zh: 」乃以謀告浚。

translations.literal: ’ Thereupon they told Jun the plot.
translations.idiomatic: They revealed the plot to Wang Jun.

sentences.zh: 浚密嚴兵，與單于圍演。

translations.literal: Jun secretly tightened troops and with the chanyu surrounded Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun secretly mobilized his forces and, with the chanyu, besieged He Yan.

sentences.zh: 演持白幡詣浚降，遂斬之，自領幽州。

translations.literal: Yan holding a white banner went to Jun to surrender; thereupon he beheaded him and himself led You Province.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan came to Wang Jun with a white flag of surrender; Wang Jun executed him anyway and took personal control of You province.

sentences.zh: 大營器械，召務勿塵，率胡晉合二萬人，進軍討穎。

translations.literal: He greatly camped weapons and tools, summoned Wuwuchen, led Hu and Jin combined twenty thousand men, advanced troops to attack Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He mass-produced arms, summoned Wuwuchen, and marched some twenty thousand Hu and Chinese troops against Sima Ying.

sentences.zh: 以主溥祁弘為前鋒，遇穎將石超于平棘，擊敗之。

translations.literal: Taking chief clerk Qi Hong as vanguard, he met Ying’s general Shi Chao at Pingji and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He made his chief clerk Qi Hong the vanguard, met Sima Ying’s general Shi Chao at Pingji, and routed him.

sentences.zh: 浚乘勝遂克鄴城，士眾暴掠，死者甚多。

translations.literal: Jun riding victory then took Ye city; soldiers and masses violently plundered; the dead were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Following up his victory he seized Ye, where his troops ran wild with looting and slaughter.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑大略婦女，浚命敢有挾藏者斬，於是沉于易水者八千人。

translations.literal: The Xianbei on a large scale seized women; Jun ordered that whoever dared hide them be beheaded; thereupon those drowned in the Yi River were eight thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei carried off women in great numbers; Wang Jun decreed death for anyone who concealed captives, and eight thousand people were drowned in the Yi River.

sentences.zh: 黔庶荼毒，自此始也。

translations.literal: The black-haired common people’s bitter poison began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The common people’s ordeal began in earnest at that point.

sentences.zh: 浚還薊，聲實益盛。

translations.literal: Jun returned to Ji; his fame and substance grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Ji, Wang Jun’s power and reputation swelled further.

sentences.zh: 東海王越將迎大駕，浚遣祁弘率烏丸突騎為先驅。

translations.literal: Prince of the Eastern Seas Yue was about to welcome the great chariot; Jun sent Qi Hong leading Wuhuan shock cavalry as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yue of Donghai prepared to escort the emperor back, Wang Jun dispatched Qi Hong at the head of Wuhuan mounted raiders as the advance guard.

sentences.zh: 惠帝旋洛陽，轉浚驃騎大將軍、都督東夷河北諸軍事，領幽州刺史，以燕國增博陵之封。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui soon went to Luoyang; Jun was transferred to Grand General of Agile Cavalry, area commander of all military affairs of the Eastern Yi and north of the He, concurrently Inspector of You Province, adding the state of Yan to Boling’s enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Hui returned to Luoyang, Wang Jun was named grand general of agile cavalry, given command of the eastern tribes and Hebei, and kept his post as inspector of You, while the principality of Yan was added to his Boling fief.

sentences.zh: 懷帝即位，以浚為司空，領烏丸校尉，務勿塵為大單于。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai ascended, Jun was made Minister of Works, concurrent Colonel of the Wuhuan, and Wuwuchen was made great chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai appointed Wang Jun minister of works and colonel of the Wuhuan, while elevating Wuwuchen to great chanyu.

sentences.zh: 浚又表封務勿塵遼西郡公，其別部大飄滑及其弟渴末別部大屠甕等皆為親晉王。

translations.literal: Jun also memorialized enfeoffing Wuwuchen as Duke of Liaoxi commandery; his separate division great Piaohua and his younger brother Kemò’s separate division great Tuweng and others all became Princes Allegiant to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun further petitioned to make Wuwuchen duke of Liaoxi and to ennoble allied chiefs such as the great Piaohua of a collateral branch and Tuweng of Kemò’s band as “princes loyal to Jin.”

sentences.zh: 永嘉中，石勒寇冀州，浚遣鮮卑文鴦討勒，勒走南陽。

translations.literal: In the Yongjia years, Shi Le raided Ji Province; Jun sent the Xianbei Wen Yang to attack Le; Le fled to Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongjia, when Shi Le invaded Ji province, Wang Jun sent the Xianbei leader Wen Yang against him and drove him toward Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 明年，勒復寇冀州，刺史王斌為勒所害，浚又領冀州。

translations.literal: The next year Le again raided Ji Province; Inspector Wang Bin was killed by Le; Jun again held Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Shi Le struck Ji again, killed Inspector Wang Bin, and Wang Jun assumed control of the province as well.

sentences.zh: 詔進浚為大司馬，加侍中、大都督、督幽冀諸軍事。

translations.literal: An edict advanced Jun to Grand Marshal, added Palace Attendant, grand area commander, commander of all military affairs of You and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The court promoted him to grand marshal, palace attendant, and overall commander of the forces of You and Ji.

sentences.zh: 使者未及發，會洛京傾覆，浚大樹威令，專征伐，遣督護王昌、中山太守阮豹等，率諸軍及務勿塵世子疾陸眷，並弟文鴦、從弟末柸，攻石勒于襄國，勒率眾來距，昌逆擊敗之。

translations.literal: Before the envoy could depart, it happened that the Luoyang capital overturned; Jun greatly set up awe-inspiring commands, monopolized punitive expeditions, sent Supervising Protector Wang Chang, Zhongshan Administrator Ruan Bao, and others, leading various armies and Wuwuchen’s heir Jilujuan, together with younger brother Wen Yang and cousin Mobai, to attack Shi Le at Xiangguo; Le led the masses to resist; Chang met and struck and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: The messenger had not yet left when Luoyang fell; Wang Jun then ruled by fiat, waging war on his own authority. He sent Wang Chang, Ruan Bao of Zhongshan, and others with allied troops, Wuwuchen’s heir Jilujuan, Jilujuan’s brothers Wen Yang and Mobai, to besiege Shi Le at Xiangguo. Shi Le marched out to meet them, but Wang Chang defeated him in the field.

sentences.zh: 末柸逐北入其壘門，為勒所獲。

translations.literal: Mobai pursued the defeated north into their rampart gate and was captured by Le.
translations.idiomatic: Mobai pursued the retreating enemy into their camp and was taken prisoner by Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 勒質末柸，遣間使來和，疾陸眷遂以鎧馬二百五十匹、金銀各一簏贖末柸，結盟而退。

translations.literal: Le held Mobai hostage, sent a secret envoy to seek peace; Jilujuan thereupon with two hundred fifty armored horses and one basket each of gold and silver ransomed Mobai, allied by oath and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le kept Mobai as a hostage until Jilujuan sent secret envoys; Jilujuan then ransomed him with two hundred fifty armored horses and baskets of gold and silver, swore a pact, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 其後浚佈告天下，稱受中詔承制，乃以司空荀藩為太尉，光祿大夫荀組為司隸，大司農華薈為太常，中書令李絙為河南尹。

translations.literal: Afterward Jun proclaimed to all under heaven, declaring he had received a mid-palace edict and held the mandate, thereupon making Minister of Works Xun Fan Grand Commandant, Grand Master of Splendid Carriage Xun Zu Metropolitan Commandant, Minister of Agriculture Hua Hui Grand Master of Ceremonies, and Palace Secretary Li Heng Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun then issued a manifesto claiming a secret imperial order and appointed Xun Fan grand commandant, Xun Zu metropolitan superintendent, Hua Hui grand master of ceremonies, and Li Heng governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 又遣祁弘討勒，及于廣宗。

translations.literal: He again sent Qi Hong to attack Le, reaching Guangzong.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Qi Hong against Shi Le again, and Qi reached Guangzong.

sentences.zh: 時大霧，弘引軍就道，卒與勒遇，為勒所殺。

translations.literal: At that time there was great fog; Hong led the army onto the road, suddenly met Le, and was killed by Le.
translations.idiomatic: A heavy fog fell; Qi Hong marched onto the road, blundered into Shi Le, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 由是劉琨與浚爭冀州。

translations.literal: Thereby Liu Kun and Jun contested Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun and Wang Jun then vied for Ji province.

sentences.zh: 琨使宗人劉希還中山合眾，代郡、上谷、廣寧三郡人皆歸於琨。

translations.literal: Kun sent clansman Liu Xi to return to Zhongshan to gather masses; the people of the three commanderies Dai, Shanggu, and Guangning all submitted to Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun sent his kinsman Liu Xi into Zhongshan to raise troops, and the populations of Dai, Shanggu, and Guangning rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 浚患之，遂輟討勒之師，而與琨相距。

translations.literal: Jun worried over this, thereupon halted the army attacking Le and opposed Kun at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Wang Jun broke off his campaign against Shi Le and turned to confront Liu Kun.

sentences.zh: 浚遣燕相胡矩督護諸軍，與疾陸眷並力攻破希。

translations.literal: Jun sent Yan Chancellor Hu Ju to supervise and protect the various armies; together with Jilujuan they joined strength and defeated Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun sent Hu Ju, chancellor of Yan, to command the allied forces; with Jilujuan he crushed Liu Xi.

sentences.zh: 驅略三郡士女出塞，琨不復能爭。

translations.literal: They drove and seized the gentry and women of the three commanderies out beyond the passes; Kun could no longer contend.
translations.idiomatic: They drove captives from the three commanderies beyond the frontier, and Liu Kun could no longer compete.

sentences.zh: 浚還，欲討勒，使棗嵩督諸軍屯易水，召疾陸眷，將與之俱攻襄國。

translations.literal: Jun returned, wished to attack Le, sent Zao Song to supervise the various armies and encamp at the Yi River, summoned Jilujuan, intending with him jointly to attack Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Wang Jun planned another strike on Shi Le, stationed Zao Song with the army on the Yi, and summoned Jilujuan for a joint assault on Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 浚為政苛暴，將吏又貪殘，並廣占山澤，引水灌田，漬陷塚墓，調發殷煩，下不堪命，多叛入鮮卑。

translations.literal: Jun’s governance was harsh and violent; generals and clerks were also greedy and cruel; together they broadly occupied mountains and marshes, led water to irrigate fields, soaking and sinking tombs; levies and drafts were abundant and troublesome; those below could not bear the commands; many rebelled and entered the Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun ruled with cruelty; his officers were rapacious. They seized hills and wetlands, diverted streams onto fields, and flooded ancestral graves, while endless levies broke the people, who fled in large numbers to the Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 從事韓咸切諫，浚怒，殺之。

translations.literal: Attendant clerk Han Xian remonstrated sharply; Jun was angry and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: His aide Han Xian remonstrated bluntly; Wang Jun had him executed in a rage.

sentences.zh: 疾陸眷自以前後違命，恐浚誅之。

translations.literal: Jilujuan himself because of before and after disobeying orders feared Jun would execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Jilujuan had repeatedly defied him and feared Wang Jun would put him to death.

sentences.zh: 勒亦遣使厚賂，疾陸眷等由是不應召。

translations.literal: Le also sent envoys with rich bribes; Jilujuan and others thereby did not respond to the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le also sent lavish gifts, so Jilujuan and his kinsmen ignored Wang Jun’s call.

sentences.zh: 浚怒，以重幣誘單于猗盧子右賢王日律孫，令攻疾陸眷，反為所破。

translations.literal: Jun was angry; with heavy gifts he enticed Chanyu Yituo’s son the Worthy King of the Right Rilüsun, ordering him to attack Jilujuan; he was on the contrary defeated by him.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Wang Jun bribed Yituo’s son, the right worthy king Rilüsun, to attack Jilujuan, but Rilüsun was beaten instead.

sentences.zh: 時劉琨大為劉聰所迫，諸避亂遊士多歸於浚。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Kun was greatly pressed by Liu Cong; various wandering gentlemen fleeing chaos mostly submitted to Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun was hard pressed by Liu Cong, and many refugee scholars flocked to Wang Jun.

sentences.zh: 浚日以強盛，乃設壇告類，建立皇太子，備置眾官。

translations.literal: Jun daily grew strong; thereupon he set up an altar to announce to the categories, established a crown prince, fully set the multitude of officials.
translations.idiomatic: As his power grew he held a ritual at the high altar, proclaimed an heir apparent, and installed a full slate of officials.

sentences.zh: 浚自領尚書令，以棗嵩、裴憲並為尚書，使其子居王宮，持節，領護匈奴中郎將，以妻舅崔毖為東夷校尉。

translations.literal: Jun himself held Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, making Zao Song and Pei Xian both Masters of Writing; he caused his son to dwell in the king’s palace, hold credentials, hold Colonel of the Xiongnu; he made his wife’s uncle Cui Bi Colonel of the Eastern Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He took the directorate of the secretariat himself, named Zao Song and Pei Xian as secretaries, installed his son in the princely residence with the imperial baton as colonel of the Xiongnu, and made his brother-in-law Cui Bi colonel of the eastern tribes.

sentences.zh: 又使嵩監司冀并兗諸軍事、行安北將軍，以田徽為兗州，李惲為青州。

translations.literal: He also caused Song to supervise military affairs of Si, Ji, Bing, and Yan, acting General Who Pacifies the North; he made Tian Hui Yan Province, Li Yun Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He put Zao Song in charge of the armies of Si, Ji, Bing, and Yan with the acting title General Who Pacifies the North, appointed Tian Hui over Yan province and Li Yun over Qing.

sentences.zh: 惲為石勒所殺，以薄盛代之。

translations.literal: Yun was killed by Shi Le; Bo Sheng replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yun fell to Shi Le and was replaced by Bo Sheng.

sentences.zh: 浚以父字處道，為「當塗高」應王者之讖，謀將僭號。

translations.literal: Jun because his father’s courtesy name was Chudao took it as ‘blocking the high road’ matching the king’s prophecy, and plotted to usurp the title.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father’s courtesy name, Chudao (“dwelling in the Way”), echoed the prophecy that “the one who blocks the high road” would become king, he plotted to seize the imperial style.

sentences.zh: 胡矩諫浚，盛陳其不可。

translations.literal: Hu Ju remonstrated with Jun, greatly stating its impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ju urged him at length not to do it.

sentences.zh: 浚忿之，出矩為魏郡守。

translations.literal: Jun resented him and sent Ju out as Administrator of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun, furious, banished him to Wei commandery as administrator.

sentences.zh: 前渤海太守劉亮、從子北海太守搏、司空掾高柔並切諫，浚怒，誅之。

translations.literal: Former Bohai Administrator Liu Liang, nephew Beihai Administrator Bo, Minister of Works clerk Gao Rou together sharply remonstrated; Jun was angry and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Former Bohai governor Liu Liang, his nephew Bo of Beihai, and ministerial clerk Gao Rou all remonstrated sharply; Wang Jun executed them in anger.

sentences.zh: 浚素不平長史燕國王悌，遂因他事殺之。

translations.literal: Jun had long been unbalanced toward Chief Clerk Wang Ti of Yan; thereupon on another matter killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He had long resented his chief clerk Wang Ti of Yan and found another pretext to kill him.

sentences.zh: 時童謠曰：「十囊五囊入棗郎。

translations.literal: At that time a children’s rhyme said, ‘Ten sacks, five sacks enter the Zao lad.’
translations.idiomatic: A children’s rhyme ran: “Bag after bag goes to Master Zao.”

sentences.zh: 」棗嵩，浚之子婿也。

translations.literal: ’ Zao Song was Jun’s son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Zao Song was Wang Jun’s son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 浚聞，責嵩而不能罪之也。

translations.literal: Jun heard, blamed Song but could not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun rebuked Zao Song but could not move against him.

sentences.zh: 又謠曰：「幽州城門似藏戶，中有伏屍王彭祖。

translations.literal: Another rhyme said, ‘You Province’s city gate is like a hidden door; within is a hidden corpse, Wang Pengzu.’
translations.idiomatic: Another rhyme said: “Ji’s gate is like a tomb; inside lies the corpse of Wang Pengzu.”

sentences.zh: 」有狐踞府門，翟雉入聽事。

translations.literal: ’ There was a fox squatting on the headquarters gate; a long-tailed pheasant entered the audience hall.
translations.idiomatic: A fox perched on the yamen gate and a pheasant walked into the audience chamber.

sentences.zh: 時燕國霍原，北州名賢，浚以僭位事示之，原不答，浚遂害之。

translations.literal: At that time Huo Yuan of Yan, a famed worthy of the northern province—Jun showed him the usurpation matter; Yuan did not answer; Jun thereupon harmed him.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Yuan of Yan was a leading scholar of the north; Wang Jun consulted him about usurpation, and when Huo Yuan refused to reply, Wang Jun had him killed.

sentences.zh: 由是士人憤怨，內外無親。

translations.literal: Thereby gentlemen were angry and resentful; within and without there were no kin.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and officials turned against him, and he had no allies left inside or out.

sentences.zh: 以矜豪日甚，不親為政，所任多苛刻；

translations.literal: Because arrogant pride daily grew extreme, he did not personally conduct governance; those appointed were mostly harsh and demanding;
translations.idiomatic: Growing ever more arrogant, he neglected government himself and staffed his regime with harsh men;

sentences.zh: 加亢旱災蝗，士卒衰弱。

translations.literal: added to severe drought disaster locusts, soldiers and troops weakened.
translations.idiomatic: drought and locusts wasted the land, and his soldiers wasted away.

sentences.zh: 浚之承制也，參佐皆內敘，唯司馬游統外出。

translations.literal: When Jun held the mandate, adjutants all received internal promotions; only Major You Tong went out on assignment.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jun assumed plenary powers, his staff were promoted at headquarters—except Major You Tong, who was posted away.

sentences.zh: 統怨，密與石勒通謀。

translations.literal: Tong resented and secretly plotted with Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: You Tong nursed a grudge and secretly dealt with Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 勒乃詐降于浚，許奉浚為主。

translations.literal: Le thereupon feigned surrender to Jun, promising to honor Jun as lord.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le pretended to submit and promised to acknowledge Wang Jun as his chief.

sentences.zh: 時百姓內叛，疾陸眷等侵逼。

translations.literal: At that time the hundred surnames rebelled within; Jilujuan and others pressed in.
translations.idiomatic: The people were rising against him, and Jilujuan’s people pressed on his borders.

sentences.zh: 浚喜勒之附己，勒遂為卑辭以事之。

translations.literal: Jun delighted in Le’s attaching to himself; Le thereupon used humble words to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun welcomed Shi Le’s allegiance, and Shi Le humored him with obsequious letters.

sentences.zh: 獻遺珍寶，使驛相繼。

translations.literal: He presented and sent precious treasures; envoys on post horses followed one another.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a stream of couriers bearing rare gifts.

sentences.zh: 浚以勒為誠，不復設備。

translations.literal: Jun took Le as sincere and no longer set defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun believed him and dropped his guard.

sentences.zh: 勒乃遣使克日上尊號於浚，浚許之。

translations.literal: Le thereupon sent envoys on a set day to offer the exalted title to Jun; Jun permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le then proposed a date to proclaim Wang Jun emperor; Wang Jun agreed.

sentences.zh: 勒屯兵易水，督護孫緯疑其詐，馳白浚，而引軍逆勒。

translations.literal: Le encamped troops at the Yi River; Supervising Protector Sun Wei suspected his deceit, galloped to report to Jun, and led troops to oppose Le.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le camped on the Yi, Supervising Protector Sun Wei smelled a trap, rode post-haste to warn Wang Jun, and led troops out to block him.

sentences.zh: 浚不聽，使勒直前。

translations.literal: Jun did not listen and caused Le to go straight forward.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun refused to listen and ordered Shi Le’s column to advance unopposed.

sentences.zh: 眾議皆曰：「胡貪而無信，必有詐，請距之。

translations.literal: The multitude’s discussion all said, ‘The Hu are greedy and without trustworthiness; there must be deceit; we beg to resist them.’
translations.idiomatic: His officers said: “The barbarians are greedy and faithless; this is a ruse—keep them out.”

sentences.zh: 」浚怒，欲斬諸言者，眾遂不敢復諫。

translations.literal: ’ Jun was angry and wished to behead those who spoke; the multitude thereupon dared not remonstrate again.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun threatened to execute anyone who objected, and they fell silent.

sentences.zh: 盛張設以待勒。

translations.literal: He lavishly spread arrangements to await Le.
translations.idiomatic: He prepared an elaborate welcome for Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 勒至城，便縱兵大掠。

translations.literal: When Le reached the city, he then unleashed troops to plunder greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le reached the walls and let his men sack the city.

sentences.zh: 浚左右復請討之，不許。

translations.literal: Jun’s attendants again begged to attack him; he did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: His entourage again begged to strike; he refused.

sentences.zh: 及勒登聽事，浚乃走出堂皇，勒眾執以見勒。

translations.literal: When Le ascended the audience hall, Jun then ran out to the bright hall; Le’s masses seized him and brought him to see Le.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le entered the audience hall, Wang Jun fled toward the inner court but was seized by Shi Le’s men and dragged before him.

sentences.zh: 勒遂與浚妻並坐，立浚於前。

translations.literal: Le thereupon sat together with Jun’s wife and stood Jun before him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le sat beside Wang Jun’s wife while Wang Jun stood before them.

sentences.zh: 浚罵曰：「胡奴調汝公，何凶逆如此！

translations.literal: Jun cursed saying, ‘Hu slave, you mock your lord—how cruel and rebellious like this!’
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun shouted: “You barbarian slave, mocking your betters—what villainy!”

sentences.zh: 」勒數浚不忠於晉，並責以百姓餒乏，積粟五十萬斛而不振給。

translations.literal: ’ Le enumerated Jun’s disloyalty to Jin and together blamed him that the hundred surnames were hungry and lacking, hoarding five hundred thousand hu of grain and not relieving and giving.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le rebuked him for betraying the Jin, hoarding five hundred thousand hu of grain while the people starved.

sentences.zh: 遂遣五百騎先送浚于襄國，收浚麾下精兵萬人，盡殺之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent five hundred cavalry first to escort Jun to Xiangguo, gathered Jun’s ten thousand picked troops under his command, and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: He sent five hundred horsemen to march Wang Jun to Xiangguo, rounded up his ten thousand elite troops, and slaughtered them.

sentences.zh: 停二日而還，孫緯遮擊之，勒僅而得免。

translations.literal: Stopping two days then returning, Sun Wei intercepted and struck them; Le barely obtained escape.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later, on the return march, Sun Wei ambushed the column and Shi Le barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 勒至襄國，斬浚，而浚竟不為之屈，大罵而死。

translations.literal: When Le reached Xiangguo, he beheaded Jun, yet Jun to the end did not yield to him, greatly cursing and dying.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangguo Shi Le executed Wang Jun, who cursed him to the last breath.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He left no heir.

sentences.zh: ，詔興滅繼絕，封沈從孫道素為博陵公。

translations.literal: , an edict raised the extinguished and continued the severed, enfeoffing Shen’s grand-nephew Daosu as Duke of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: The court issued an edict to restore fallen houses and enfeoffed Wang Shen’s great-grandnephew Wang Daosu as duke of Boling.

sentences.zh: 卒，子崇之嗣。

translations.literal: He died; son Chongzhi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son Wang Chongzhi inherited the title.

sentences.zh: ，改封東莞郡公。

translations.literal: , changed enfeoffment to Duke of Dongguan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The fief was later changed to duke of Dongguan commandery.

sentences.zh: 宋受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Song received the abdication, the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liu-Song dynasty took the throne, the noble house was struck off.

sentences.zh: 荀顗

translations.literal: Xun Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Xun Yi.

sentences.zh: 荀顗，字景倩，潁川人，魏太尉彧之第六子也。

translations.literal: Xun Yi, courtesy name Jingqian, a man of Yingchuan, was Wei Grand Commandant Yu’s sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yi, courtesy name Jingqian, came from Yingchuan and was the sixth son of Wei’s grand commandant Xun Yu.

sentences.zh: 幼為姊婿陳群所賞。

translations.literal: In youth he was appreciated by his elder sister’s husband Chen Qun.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he won the esteem of his brother-in-law Chen Qun.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，總角知名，博學洽聞，理思周密。

translations.literal: By nature supremely filial, in tied-hair youth he had a clear name; broadly learned and comprehensive in hearing, his reasoning thought was thorough and dense.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply filial, famous even as a child, widely read, and precise in argument.

sentences.zh: 魏時以父勳除中郎。

translations.literal: In Wei times by his father’s merit he was appointed gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei he received a gentleman’s appointment on his father’s merit.

sentences.zh: 宣帝輔政，見顗奇之，曰：「荀令君之子也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan assisted governance, seeing Yi he deemed him extraordinary, saying, ‘He is Minister Xun’s son.’
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yi held power he met Xun Yi, marveled at him, and said, “This is the son of Director Xun.”

sentences.zh: 」擢拜散騎侍郎，累遷侍中。

translations.literal: ’ He was promoted and appointed Gentleman Cavalier Attendant, promoted in stages to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to gentleman cavalier attendant and eventually to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 為魏少帝執經，拜騎都尉，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: For Wei’s young emperor he held the classics; he was appointed Commandant of Cavalry and granted noble rank Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: He tutored the Wei young emperor in the classics, was named commandant of cavalry, and received the rank of marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 難鍾會《易》無互體，又與扶風王駿論仁孝孰先，見稱於世。

translations.literal: He challenged Zhong Hui’s *Changes* having no interlocking forms; also with Prince of Fufeng Jun he debated whether benevolence or filial piety came first; he was praised in the age.
translations.idiomatic: He disputed Zhong Hui’s view that the *Zhou yi* lacked “interlocking” trigrams, debated with Sima Jun of Fufeng whether benevolence or filial duty took precedence, and won renown.

sentences.zh: 時曹爽專權，何晏等欲害太常傅嘏，顗營救得免。

translations.literal: At that time Cao Shuang monopolized power; He Yan and others wished to harm Grand Master of Ceremonies Fu Gu; Yi worked rescue and he obtained escape.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Shuang dominated the court, He Yan and his faction moved against Fu Gu; Xun Yi intervened and saved him.

sentences.zh: 及高貴鄉公立，顗言于景帝曰：「今上踐阼，權道非常，宜速遣使宣德四方，且察外志。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Gaoguixiang was established, Yi spoke to Emperor Jing saying, ‘Now the superior ascends the throne; the way of power is not ordinary; it is fitting quickly to dispatch envoys to spread virtue to the four directions, and also observe outer intentions.’
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Mao came to the throne, Xun Yi told Sima Shi: “The new ruler’s accession is irregular; send envoys at once to proclaim your policy in every quarter and to gauge regional loyalties.”

sentences.zh: 」毌丘儉、文欽果不服，舉兵反。

translations.literal: ’ Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin indeed did not submit and raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin soon rose in revolt, just as he had warned.

sentences.zh: 顗預討儉等有功，進爵萬歲亭侯，邑四百戶。

translations.literal: Yi participated in punishing Jian and others with merit; advanced in noble rank to Marquis of Wansui village, fief four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his part in suppressing the rebels he was advanced to marquis of Wansui hamlet with four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 文帝輔政，遷尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen assisted governance, he was promoted to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Zhao directed the government, Xun Yi was promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 帝征諸葛誕，留顗鎮守。

translations.literal: The emperor campaigned against Zhuge Dan; Yi was left to guard and hold.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao left him in charge at the capital during the campaign against Zhuge Dan.

sentences.zh: 顗甥陳泰卒，顗代泰為僕射，領吏部，四辭而後就職。

translations.literal: Yi’s maternal nephew Chen Tai died; Yi replaced Tai as Vice Director, holding the Ministry of Personnel; four times declining then took office.
translations.idiomatic: When his nephew Chen Tai died, Xun Yi succeeded him as vice director of the secretariat and head of the Ministry of Personnel after four refusals.

sentences.zh: 顗承泰後，加之淑慎，綜核名實，風俗澄正。

translations.literal: Yi succeeding after Tai, added to this virtuous caution, synthesizing and examining name and substance; custom and transformation were clear and correct.
translations.idiomatic: Building on Chen Tai’s work, he ran the ministry with scrupulous care, matching appointments to real merit, and official conduct grew sound.

sentences.zh: 咸熙中，遷司空，進爵鄉侯。

translations.literal: In the Xianxi years he was promoted Minister of Works, advanced in noble rank to village marquis.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianxi he became minister of works and was raised to village marquis.

sentences.zh: 顗年逾耳順，孝養蒸蒸，以母憂去職，毀幾滅性，海內稱之。

translations.literal: Yi’s years passed ear-compliance; filial nurturing steamed upward; by mother’s mourning he left office; emaciation nearly extinguished nature; within the seas praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Past sixty, he cared for his parents with exemplary devotion; when mourning his mother he resigned and nearly wasted away—people everywhere praised him.

sentences.zh: 文帝奏，宜依漢太傅胡廣喪母故事，給司空吉凶導從。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen memorialized: it is fitting to follow Han Grand Tutor Hu Guang’s mother’s mourning precedent, supplying the Minister of Works auspicious and inauspicious guides and followers.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao petitioned that, following the Han precedent for Hu Guang, the minister of works be granted full funeral escorts for both mourning and celebratory occasions.

sentences.zh: 及蜀平，興復五等，命顗定禮儀。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, the five ranks were raised and restored; he ordered Yi to fix ritual and ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell and the five noble ranks were revived, he was charged with drafting court ritual.

sentences.zh: 顗上請羊祜、任愷、庾峻、應貞、孔顥共刪改舊文，撰定晉禮。

translations.literal: Yi submitted requesting Yang Hu, Ren Kai, Yu Jun, Ying Zhen, Kong Hao jointly to delete and revise old texts, compile and fix Jin ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Yang Hu, Ren Kai, Yu Jun, Ying Zhen, and Kong Hao to revise old precedents and codify Jin dynasty ritual.

sentences.zh: 咸熙初，封臨淮侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianxi, he was enfeoffed Marquis of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianxi he was made marquis of Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼，進爵為公，食邑一千八百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, he advanced in noble rank to duke, eating fief one thousand eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yan took the throne, Xun Yi was raised to duke with a fief of eighteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「昔禹命九官，契敷五教，所以弘崇王化，示人軌儀也。

translations.literal: Again an edict said, ‘Formerly Yu ordered the nine officials; Xie spread the five teachings; this was the means to enlarge and honor kingly transformation, showing people norms and models.’
translations.idiomatic: Another edict declared: “When Yu appointed the nine ministers and Xie spread the five teachings, it was to magnify royal civilization and give the people a model.”

sentences.zh: 朕承洪業，昧于大道，思訓五品，以康四海。

translations.literal: I inherit the vast enterprise, am dark to the great way, think to instruct the five grades, thereby to bring peace to the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: I have received a great mandate yet am still learning the Way; I wish to instruct the five relationships and bring peace to the realm.

sentences.zh: 侍中、司空顗，明允篤誠，思心通遠，翼亮先皇，遂輔朕躬，實有佐命弼導之勳。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant, Minister of Works Yi is enlightened, trustworthy, sincere and earnest, his thinking penetrates the distant, wing-brightened the former emperor, then assisted my person; truly he has merit as assistant to the mandate and guide.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant and Minister of Works Xun Yi is discerning, loyal, and farsighted; he aided my late father and now supports me—true architect of our succession.

sentences.zh: 宜掌教典，以隆時雍。

translations.literal: It is fitting he grasp the teaching canons, thereby to exalt the age’s harmony.
translations.idiomatic: He should oversee moral education and help harmonize the age.

sentences.zh: 其以顗為司徒。

translations.literal: Let Yi be made Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint Xun Yi minister of education.

sentences.zh: 」尋加侍中，遷太尉、都督城外牙門諸軍事，置司馬親兵百人。

translations.literal: ’ Soon added Palace Attendant, promoted to Grand Commandant, area commander of all military affairs of the outer gate halberds, established Major personal troops one hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was again palace attendant, promoted to grand commandant, given command of the outer garrisons, and allowed a staff major with a hundred household guards.

sentences.zh: 頃之，又詔曰：「侍中、太尉顗，溫恭忠允，至行純備，博古洽聞，耆艾不殆。

translations.literal: Shortly, again an edict said, ‘Palace Attendant, Grand Commandant Yi is warm, respectful, loyal, and trustworthy; utmost conduct pure and complete; broadly ancient, comprehensive in hearing; old age not failing.’
translations.idiomatic: A further edict read: “Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant Xun Yi is gentle, reverent, and loyal; his conduct is flawless; he is learned and still vigorous in old age.”

sentences.zh: 其以公行太子太傅，侍中、太尉如故。」

translations.literal: Let the duke act as Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince; Palace Attendant, Grand Commandant as before.’
translations.idiomatic: Let him serve as grand tutor to the heir apparent while retaining his posts as palace attendant and grand commandant.”

sentences.zh: 時以《正德》、《大豫》雅頌未合，命顗定樂。

translations.literal: At the time because *Zhengde* and *Dayu* hymns and eulogies did not match, he ordered Yi to fix the music.
translations.idiomatic: Because the court hymns *Zhengde* and *Dayu* did not harmonize, he was ordered to revise the ritual music.

sentences.zh: 事未終，以薨。

translations.literal: The affair not finished, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died before the work was done.

sentences.zh: 帝為舉哀，皇太子臨喪，二宮賻贈，禮秩有加。

translations.literal: The emperor for him raised mourning; the crown prince attended the funeral; the two palaces gave burial gifts; ritual rank had additions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him, the crown prince attended the obsequies, and both palaces sent rich funeral gifts beyond the usual rank.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「侍中、太尉、行太子太傅、臨淮公顗，清純體道，忠允立朝，歷司外內，茂績既崇，訓傅東宮，徽猷弘著，可謂行歸於周，有始有卒者矣。

translations.literal: An edict said, ‘Palace Attendant, Grand Commandant, acting Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince, Duke of Linhuai Yi, pure and embodying the way, loyal and trustworthy standing at court, passed through offices outer and inner, lush merit already lofty, instructing and tutoring the Eastern Palace, fine planning broadly manifest—may be called conduct returning to Zhou, having beginning and having end.’
translations.idiomatic: The edict praised him: “Palace Attendant, Grand Commandant, acting grand tutor, Duke of Linhuai—pure in mind and faithful in service, he served both court and camp, achieved great deeds, and instructed the heir with distinction; his life matched the ancient standard from first to last.”

sentences.zh: 不幸薨殂，朕甚痛之。

translations.literal: Unluckily he died; I greatly grieve him.
translations.idiomatic: His death is a heavy blow to me.

sentences.zh: 其賜溫明秘器、朝服一具，衣一襲。

translations.literal: Let there be bestowed warm-bright secret goods, one set of court dress, one suit of clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Grant him the jade-lined burial coffin, one full set of court robes, and another suit.

sentences.zh: 諡曰康。

translations.literal: Posthumous name Kang.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title is Kang (“Peaceful”).

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「太尉不恤私門，居無館宇，素絲之志，沒而彌顯。

translations.literal: ’ Again an edict said, ‘The Grand Commandant did not pity his private gate; dwelling without mansion halls; plain silk’s intent, in death yet more manifest.’
translations.idiomatic: Another edict noted: “The grand commandant ignored his own household, owned no fine residence, and his integrity shines all the brighter now that he is gone.”

sentences.zh: 其賜家錢二百萬，使立宅舍。

translations.literal: Let his household be given two million cash, causing them to establish a residence.’
translations.idiomatic: Give his family two million cash to build a proper house.”

sentences.zh: 」咸寧初，詔論次功臣，將配饗宗廟。

translations.literal: ’ At the beginning of Xianning, an edict discussed ordering merit ministers, intending to join them in feasting the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianning the court ranked the founding ministers for enshrinement in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 所司奏顗等十二人銘功太常，配饗清廟。

translations.literal: The responsible offices memorialized Yi and twelve others to inscribe merit at Grand Master of Ceremonies, to join feasting at the Clear Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry listed Xun Yi and eleven others to have their deeds recorded by the court of imperial sacrifices and to receive offerings in the high temple.

sentences.zh: 顗明《三禮》，知朝廷大儀，而無質直之操，唯阿意苟合于荀勖、賈充之間。

translations.literal: Yi understood the *Three Rites*, knew the court’s great ceremonies, but lacked plain and straight conduct; only fawned on intent and compromised between Xun Xu and Jia Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yi mastered the *Three Rites* and court ritual, yet lacked moral backbone, currying favor with Xun Xu and Jia Chong.

sentences.zh: 初，皇太子將納妃，顗上言賈充女姿德淑茂，可以參選，以此獲譏於世。

translations.literal: At first, when the crown prince was about to take a consort, Yi submitted words that Jia Chong’s daughter’s bearing and virtue were pure and lush, could join selection; by this obtained ridicule in the world.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir was choosing a bride, Xun Yi praised Jia Chong’s daughter as virtuous and fit for selection, for which contemporaries mocked him.

sentences.zh: 顗無子，以從孫徽嗣。

translations.literal: Yi had no son; he took cousin’s grandson Hui to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, he named his grandnephew Xun Hui as heir.

sentences.zh: 中興初，以顗兄玄孫序為顗後，封臨淮公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Restoration, he took Yi’s elder brother’s great-great-grandson Xu as Yi’s successor, enfeoffing Duke of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Jin restoration a great-grandnephew of Xun Yi’s elder brother, Xun Xu, was made his heir and enfeoffed as duke of Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 序卒，又絕，孝武帝又封序子恆繼顗後。

translations.literal: Xu died, again cut off; Emperor Xiaowu again enfeoffed Xu’s son Heng to continue Yi’s succession.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun Xu died without issue, Emperor Xiaowu made his son Xun Heng the next heir to Xun Yi’s line.

sentences.zh: 恆卒，子龍符嗣。

translations.literal: Heng died; son Longfu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Heng was succeeded by his son Xun Longfu.

sentences.zh: 宋受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Song received the abdication, the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Liu-Song accession ended the noble line.

sentences.zh: 荀勖

translations.literal: Xun Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Xun Xu.

sentences.zh: 荀勖，字公曾，潁川潁陰人，漢司空爽曾孫也。

translations.literal: Xun Xu, courtesy name Gongzeng, a man of Yingyin in Yingchuan, was Han Minister of Works Shuang’s great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu, courtesy name Gongzeng, came from Yingyin in Yingchuan and was a great-grandson of the Han minister of works Xun Shuang.

sentences.zh: 祖棐，射聲校尉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fei was Colonel of Archers Who Sound the Shot.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xun Fei had been colonel of the skilled archers.

sentences.zh: 父肸，早亡。

translations.literal: His father Xi died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xun Xi died while he was still young.

sentences.zh: 勖依于舅氏。

translations.literal: Xu relied on his mother’s clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised by his mother’s family.

sentences.zh: 岐嶷夙成，年十餘歲能屬文。

translations.literal: He was precocious and early completed; at age over ten sui able to compose texts.
translations.idiomatic: Precocious, he could write polished essays before he was fifteen.

sentences.zh: 從外祖魏太傅鍾繇曰：「此兒當及其曾祖。

translations.literal: His maternal grandfather Wei Grand Tutor Zhong Yao said, ‘This child will match his great-grandfather.’
translations.idiomatic: His maternal grandfather, Wei grand tutor Zhong Yao, said, “This boy will rival his great-grandfather.”

sentences.zh: 」既長，遂博學，達于從政。

translations.literal: ’ When grown, then broadly learned, penetrating in following governance.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he became widely read and adept at administration.

sentences.zh: 仕魏，辟大將軍曹爽掾，遷中書通事郎。

translations.literal: Serving Wei, he was summoned as Grand General Cao Shuang’s clerk, promoted to Palace Secretariat General Affairs Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei he entered Cao Shuang’s staff as a clerk and rose to a secretariat post handling routine memorials.

sentences.zh: 爽誅，門生故吏無敢往者，勖獨臨赴，眾乃從之。

translations.literal: When Shuang was executed, disciples and former subordinates none dared go; Xu alone attended the funeral; the masses then followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Shuang was executed, his former followers dared not mourn him; Xun Xu alone went, and others then followed his example.

sentences.zh: 為安陽令，轉驃騎從事中郎。

translations.literal: He was Anyang magistrate, transferred to Attendant Clerk of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Anyang, then became an aide on the staff of the General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 勖有遺愛，安陽生為立祠。

translations.literal: Xu had leftover love; Anyang students for him established a shrine.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Anyang loved him and built a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 遷廷尉正，參文帝大將軍軍事，賜爵關內侯，轉從事中郎，領記室。

translations.literal: He was promoted Rectifier of the Commandant of Justice, joined Emperor Wen’s Grand General’s military affairs, granted noble rank Marquis Within the Passes, transferred to Attendant Clerk, holding the records office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to senior judge in the ministry of justice, joined Sima Zhao’s military staff, received the rank of marquis within the passes, and became an aide in charge of the headquarters secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高貴鄉公欲為變時，大將軍掾孫佑等守閶闔門。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Gaoguixiang wished to make a coup, Grand General clerk Sun You and others guarded the Changhe Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Mao planned his coup, Sun You and other aides of the grand general held the Changhe Gate.

sentences.zh: 帝弟安陽侯榦聞難欲入，佑謂榦曰：「未有入者，可從東掖門。

translations.literal: The emperor’s younger brother Marquis of Anyang Gan heard the crisis and wished to enter; You said to Gan, ‘There is none who has entered; you may go from the eastern side gate.’
translations.idiomatic: Cao Mao’s brother Cao Gan tried to rush in; Sun You told him, “No one has entered yet—use the eastern side gate.”

sentences.zh: 」及榦至，帝遲之，榦以狀白，帝欲族誅佑。

translations.literal: ’ When Gan arrived, the emperor delayed him; Gan reported the situation; the emperor wished to clan-execute You.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Gan arrived too late and explained what Sun You had done; Sima Zhao wanted to exterminate Sun You’s entire clan.

sentences.zh: 勖諫曰：「孫佑不納安陽，誠宜深責。

translations.literal: Xu remonstrated saying, ‘Sun You not admitting Anyang is truly fitting to blame deeply.’
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu argued: “Sun You certainly deserves harsh blame for turning Cao Gan away.”

sentences.zh: 然事有逆順，用刑不可以喜怒為輕重。

translations.literal: Yet affairs have contrary and compliant; applying punishment cannot take joy and anger as light and heavy.
translations.idiomatic: But justice must follow the rights of the case, not the ruler’s mood.

sentences.zh: 今成倅刑止其身，佑乃族誅，恐義士私議。

translations.literal: Now Cheng Cui’s punishment stops at his person; You then clan execution—fear righteous gentlemen private discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Cui was punished only in his own person; to wipe out Sun You’s whole clan would shock fair-minded men.”

sentences.zh: 」乃免佑為庶人。

translations.literal: ’ Thereupon spared You as commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Sun You was reduced to commoner status instead.

sentences.zh: 時官騎路遺求為刺客入蜀，勖言於帝曰：「明公以至公宰天下，宜杖正義以伐違貳。

translations.literal: At that time official cavalry Lu Yi sought to be assassin entering Shu; Xu spoke to the emperor saying, ‘The enlightened duke by utmost fairness rules all under heaven; it is fitting to wield righteous justice to punish rebellion and division.’
translations.idiomatic: When a guardsman named Lu Yi volunteered to assassinate someone in Shu, Xun Xu told Sima Zhao: “You rule by fairness; you should strike rebels with open justice.”

sentences.zh: 而名以刺客除賊，非所謂刑于四海，以德服遠也。

translations.literal: Yet to name assassin to remove rebels is not what is called displaying punishment to the four seas, by virtue subduing the distant.’
translations.idiomatic: “Hired murder is not how you teach the empire law or win the far lands by virtue.”

sentences.zh: 」帝稱善。

translations.literal: ’ The emperor praised it good.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao agreed.

sentences.zh: 及鍾會謀反，審問未至，而外人先告之。

translations.literal: When Zhong Hui plotted rebellion, the interrogation had not yet arrived, but outsiders first reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Word of Zhong Hui’s rebellion reached the court before official confirmation.

sentences.zh: 帝待會素厚，未之信也。

translations.literal: The emperor toward Hui had always been generous; did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao had long favored Zhong Hui and refused to believe the report.

sentences.zh: 勖曰：「會雖受恩，然其性未可許以見得思義，不可不速為之備。

translations.literal: Xu said, ‘Hui though receiving favor, yet his nature cannot be permitted to see gain and think of righteousness; cannot but quickly for him make preparations.’
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu said: “Zhong Hui may be favored, but he is not the sort to choose duty over gain—we must arm against him at once.”

sentences.zh: 」帝即出鎮長安，主簿郭奕、參軍王深以勖是會從甥，少長舅氏，勸帝斥出之。
