translations.literal: ’ The emperor immediately went out to garrison Chang’an; chief clerk Guo Yi, staff officer Wang Shen because Xu was Hui’s cousin’s son, young and raised by mother’s clan, urged the emperor to expel him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao set out for Chang’an. Guo Yi and Wang Shen noted that Xun Xu was Zhong Hui’s cousin and had grown up in Zhong’s household, and urged his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 帝不納，而使勖陪乘，待之如初。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept but caused Xu to accompany the chariot, treating him as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao refused, kept Xun Xu in his carriage as before, and trusted him as ever.

sentences.zh: 先是，勖啟「伐蜀，宜以衛瓘為監軍」。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xu had submitted, “Attacking Shu, it is fitting to make Wei Guan supervising army.”
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xun Xu had recommended Wei Guan as army supervisor for the Shu campaign.

sentences.zh: 及蜀中亂，賴瓘以濟。

translations.literal: When Shu interior was in chaos, relied on Guan to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu erupted in mutiny, Wei Guan’s steadiness saved the situation.

sentences.zh: 會平，還洛，與裴秀、羊祜共管機密。

translations.literal: When Hui was pacified, returned to Luoyang, together with Pei Xiu, Yang Hu jointly managed secret essentials.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhong Hui fell he returned to Luoyang and, with Pei Xiu and Yang Hu, directed confidential affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 時將發使聘吳，並遣當時文士作書與孫皓，帝用勖所作。

translations.literal: At the time about to dispatch envoys to visit Wu, together sending the age’s literary men to compose letters to Sun Hao; the emperor used what Xu composed.
translations.idiomatic: When envoys were sent to Wu, leading scholars each drafted letters to Sun Hao; Sima Zhao chose Xun Xu’s version.

sentences.zh: 皓既報命和親，帝謂勖曰：「君前作書，使吳思順，勝十萬之眾也。

translations.literal: When Hao had returned mission harmonizing kinship, the emperor said to Xu, ‘Your lord earlier composed the letter, causing Wu to think of submission—it surpasses a hundred thousand troops.’
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Hao replied favorably, Sima Zhao told him, “Your letter did more to bring Wu to heel than an army of a hundred thousand.”

sentences.zh: 」帝即晉王位，以勖為侍中，封安陽子，邑千戶。

translations.literal: ’ The emperor then assumed the Jin king’s position, making Xu Palace Attendant, enfeoffing him Marquis of Anyang, fief one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yan took the title of king of Jin, Xun Xu became palace attendant and marquis of Anyang with a thousand-household fief.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，改封濟北郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, changed enfeoffment to Duke of Jibei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Yan’s accession the fief was raised to duke of Jibei commandery.

sentences.zh: 勖以羊祜讓，乃固辭為侯。

translations.literal: Xu because Yang Hu yielded, thereupon firmly declined to be duke and was marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Following Yang Hu’s example he insisted on remaining a mere marquis.

sentences.zh: 拜中書監，加侍中，領著作，與賈充共定律令。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat, added Palace Attendant, held composition, together with Jia Chong jointly fixed statutes and orders.
translations.idiomatic: He was named director of the secretariat with concurrent posts as palace attendant and chief compiler, and with Jia Chong codified the legal code.

sentences.zh: 充將鎮關右也，勖謂馮紞曰：「賈公遠放，吾等失勢。

translations.literal: When Chong was about to garrison the Guan west, Xu said to Feng Dan, ‘Lord Jia far banished, we lose power.’
translations.idiomatic: When Jia Chong was ordered to the northwest, Xun Xu told Feng Dan, “If he leaves the capital we lose our footing.”

sentences.zh: 太子婚尚未定，若使充女得為妃，則不留而自停矣。

translations.literal: The crown prince’s marriage is not yet fixed; if we cause Chong’s daughter to become consort, then without staying it will stop of itself.’
translations.idiomatic: “The heir’s marriage is still open—if Jia Chong’s daughter enters the Eastern Palace, his transfer will be dropped.”

sentences.zh: 」勖與紞伺帝間並稱「充女才色絕世，若納東宮，必能輔佐君子，有《關雎》后妃之德。

translations.literal: ’ Xu and Dan watched the emperor’s leisure and together praised, ‘Chong’s daughter’s talent and beauty are unmatched in the age; if taken into the Eastern Palace, she will surely be able to assist the gentleman, having the *Guan ju* consorts’ virtue.’
translations.idiomatic: They waited on Sima Yan’s mood and praised Jia Chong’s daughter as incomparably gifted and beautiful, fit for the heir and worthy of the virtuous queens praised in the *Guan ju* ode.”

sentences.zh: 」遂成婚。

translations.literal: ’ Thereupon the marriage was completed.
translations.idiomatic: The match was made.

sentences.zh: 當時甚為正直者所疾，而獲佞媚之譏焉。

translations.literal: At the time he was greatly hated by the upright, and obtained sycophancy’s ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: Men of principle despised him, and he was mocked as a flatterer.

sentences.zh: 久之，進位光祿大夫。

translations.literal: After long time, advanced in rank to Grand Master of Splendid Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was promoted to grand master of splendid carriage.

sentences.zh: 既掌樂事，又修律呂，並行於世。

translations.literal: Having grasped music affairs, also repaired pitch pipes; both practiced in the age.
translations.idiomatic: As director of music he recalibrated the pitch standards, and his system was adopted at court.

sentences.zh: 初，勖于路逢趙賈人牛鐸，識其聲。

translations.literal: At first, Xu on the road met a Zhao merchant’s ox bell and recognized its sound.
translations.idiomatic: Once on the road he heard an ox bell from a Zhao merchant and remembered its tone.

sentences.zh: 及掌樂，音韻未調，乃曰：「得趙之牛鐸則諧矣。

translations.literal: When he grasped music, tones were not tuned; then said, ‘Obtaining Zhao’s ox bell then harmonious.’
translations.idiomatic: When court pitch proved out of tune, he said, “We need that Zhao ox bell to match the scale.”

sentences.zh: 」遂下郡國，悉送牛鐸，果得諧者。

translations.literal: ’ Thereupon ordered commanderies and kingdoms, all to send ox bells; indeed obtained harmonious ones.
translations.idiomatic: Orders went to every commandery to send ox bells until the matching tone was found.

sentences.zh: 又嘗在帝坐進飯，謂在坐人曰：「此是勞薪所炊。

translations.literal: Also once at the emperor’s seat advancing food, said to those seated, ‘This is labor firewood cooked.’
translations.idiomatic: At an imperial meal he told the company, “This rice was cooked over seasoned firewood.”

sentences.zh: 」咸未之信。

translations.literal: ’ All did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: No one believed him.

sentences.zh: 帝遣問膳夫，乃云：「實用故車腳。

translations.literal: The emperor sent to ask the cook; then said, ‘Truly used old cart axles.’
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned the cook, who admitted using old cart axles for fuel.

sentences.zh: 」舉世伏其明識。

translations.literal: ’ All the age submitted to his clear knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: The court marveled at his acuity.

sentences.zh: 俄領秘書監，與中書令張華依劉向《別錄》，整理記籍。

translations.literal: Soon he held Director of the Palace Library, together with Palace Secretary Zhang Hua following Liu Xiang’s *Separate Catalogue*, arranging and ordering records and registers.
translations.idiomatic: He soon directed the imperial library and, with Zhang Hua, reorganized the archives on the model of Liu Xiang’s *Bielu*.

sentences.zh: 又立書博士，置弟子教習，以鐘、胡為法。

translations.literal: Also established calligraphy erudites, set disciples to teach and practice, taking Zhong and Hu as models.
translations.idiomatic: He founded professorships in calligraphy with students drilled in the styles of Zhong Yao and Hu Zhao.

sentences.zh: 咸寧初，與石苞等並為佐命功臣，列于銘饗。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianning, together with Shi Bao and others were merit ministers assistant to the mandate, listed in inscribed feasting.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianning he was named among the founding meritocrats honored in the temple inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 及王浚表請伐吳，勖與賈充固諫不可，帝不從，而吳果滅。

translations.literal: When Wang Jun memorialized requesting to attack Wu, Xu and Jia Chong firmly remonstrated it could not be done; the emperor did not follow, yet Wu was indeed destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jun, the general who would lead the river assault on Wu, urged that campaign, Xun Xu and Jia Chong strongly opposed it; the emperor overruled them, and Wu fell as planned.

sentences.zh: 以專典詔命，論功封子一人為亭侯，邑一千戶，賜絹千匹。

translations.literal: Because he solely managed edicts and commands, by merit discussion enfeoffed one son as village marquis, fief one thousand households, bestowed one thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: For his monopoly on drafting imperial orders, one son was enfeoffed as village marquis with a thousand households and a thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 又封孫顯為潁陽亭侯。

translations.literal: Also enfeoffed Sun Xian as Marquis of Yingyang village.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Xian was also enfeoffed as marquis of Yingyang hamlet.

sentences.zh: 及得汲郡塚中古文竹書，詔勖撰次之，以為《中經》，列在秘書。

translations.literal: When obtained Ji commandery tomb’s ancient text bamboo books, edict ordered Xu to compile and order them, making *Central Canon*, listed in the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the ancient bamboo texts were recovered from a Ji commandery tomb, he was ordered to edit them into the *Zhong jing* collection in the palace library.

sentences.zh: 時議遣王公之國，帝以問勖，勖對曰：「諸王公已為都督，而使之國，則廢方任。

translations.literal: At the time discussing dispatching princes and dukes to their states, the emperor used this to ask Xu; Xu replied saying, ‘The various princes and dukes already are area commanders; yet causing them to go to their states then abolishes regional duty.’
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated sending imperial princes to their fiefs, Xun Xu answered: “They already hold regional commands; packing them off to their kingdoms would strip those posts.”

sentences.zh: 又分割郡縣，人心戀本，必用嗷嗷。

translations.literal: Also splitting apart commanderies and counties, people’s hearts cling to roots; surely will be wailing.
translations.idiomatic: Carving up commanderies would uproot people attached to their homes and provoke widespread outcry.

sentences.zh: 國皆置軍，官兵還當給國，而闕邊守。

translations.literal: States all set armies; officers and soldiers returning ought supply the states, yet lack border defense.
translations.idiomatic: Each princely state would need troops drawn from the regular army, weakening frontier garrisons.

sentences.zh: 」帝重使勖思之，勖又陳曰：「如詔准古方伯選才，使軍國各隨方面為都督，誠如明旨。

translations.literal: ’ The emperor again had Xu ponder it; Xu again stated saying, ‘As the edict aligns with ancient regional lords selecting talent, causing army and state each follow direction as area commander—truly as the enlightened decree.’
translations.idiomatic: Asked again, he said: “Your plan to revive classical regional governors and align military with geographic commands is sound.”

sentences.zh: 至於割正封疆。

translations.literal: As to cutting and correcting sealed boundaries.
translations.idiomatic: But redrawing territorial boundaries

sentences.zh: 使親疏不同誠為佳矣。

translations.literal: causing close and distant not the same is truly excellent.
translations.idiomatic: to separate princes of the blood from more distant nobles would indeed be ideal

sentences.zh: 然分裂舊土，猶懼多所搖動，必使人心聰擾，思惟竊宜如前。

translations.literal: Yet splitting apart old lands, still fear much shaking; surely will cause people’s hearts clever-disturbed; privately think it is fitting as before.
translations.idiomatic: yet dismantling existing provinces would unsettle the realm and stir popular unrest; I would rather keep the present arrangement.”

sentences.zh: 若于事不得不時有所轉封，而不至分割土域，有所損奪者，可隨宜節度。

translations.literal: If in affairs unavoidably from time to time there is transfer of enfeoffment, yet not reaching splitting land domains, having something stripped—may follow what is fitting and moderate.
translations.idiomatic: If transfers of fiefs become unavoidable, do them case by case without carving up whole territories or seizing land wholesale.”

sentences.zh: 其五等體國經遠，實不成制度。

translations.literal: As for the five ranks embodying the state and threading the distant, truly do not complete the system.
translations.idiomatic: “The five ranks of nobility look impressive for the long term but do not yet form a workable system.”

sentences.zh: 然但虛名，其於實事，略與舊郡縣鄉亭無異。

translations.literal: Yet only empty name; as to real affairs, roughly with old commanderies, counties, townships, and posts no different.
translations.idiomatic: In practice they are hollow titles—administration stays much like the old commandery, county, and township setup.”

sentences.zh: 若造次改奪，恐不能不以為恨。

translations.literal: If hastily changing and seizing, fear cannot but take it as resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Sudden revocations would breed lasting resentment.”

sentences.zh: 今方了其大者，以為五等可須後裁度。

translations.literal: Now just finishing its great parts; I think the five ranks may await later measuring and cutting.
translations.idiomatic: We are still settling larger issues; the five-rank system can wait for a later decision.”

sentences.zh: 凡事雖有久而益善者，若臨時或有不解，亦不可忽。

translations.literal: In general affairs though there are those long yet more good; if facing the time perhaps there is not understanding, also cannot be neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Some reforms improve with time, but anything we do not fully grasp must not be rushed.”

sentences.zh: 」帝以勖言為允，多從其意。

translations.literal: ’ The emperor took Xu’s words as fitting, mostly followed his intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged his advice sound and largely followed it.

sentences.zh: 時又議省州郡縣半吏以赴農功，勖議以為：

translations.literal: At the time again discussing saving half the clerks of provinces, commanderies, and counties to hasten agricultural work, Xu’s deliberation held:
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated halving local clerks to free labor for farming, Xun Xu submitted:

sentences.zh: 勖論議損益多此類。

translations.literal: Xu’s discussions of harm and benefit were mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his policy papers balanced reform and caution in this vein.

sentences.zh: 太康中詔曰：「勖明哲聰達，經識天序，有佐命之功，兼博洽之才。

translations.literal: In the Taikang years an edict said, ‘Xu is wise, enlightened, clever and penetrating, classic-knowing heaven’s order, has merit assisting the mandate, concurrently broadly comprehensive talent.’
translations.idiomatic: A Taikang-era edict declared: “Xun Xu is discerning, quick-witted, versed in cosmic pattern, a founding meritocrat, and a scholar of wide learning.”

sentences.zh: 久典內任，著勳弘茂，詢事考言，謀猷允誠。

translations.literal: Long managing inner posts, his displayed merit is vast and lush; inquiring affairs and examining words, planning and counsel trustworthy and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: Long entrusted with inner-court duties, he has earned great merit, weighs counsel carefully, and serves with loyal judgment.

sentences.zh: 宜登大位，毗贊朝政。

translations.literal: He should ascend a great position, assist and praise court governance.
translations.idiomatic: He should take higher office and help steer the government.

sentences.zh: 今以勖為光祿大夫、儀同三司、開府辟召，守中書監、侍中、侯如故。

translations.literal: Now making Xu Grand Master of Splendid Carriage, ceremonial equal to the Three Dukes, with independent recruitment, retaining Director of the Palace Secretariat, Palace Attendant, and marquis as before.
translations.idiomatic: He is named grand master of splendid carriage with three-ducal honors and the right to open his own bureau, while keeping the secretariat directorship, palace attendant post, and marquisate.

sentences.zh: 」時太尉賈充、司徒李胤並薨，太子太傅又缺，勖表陳：「三公保傅，宜得其人。

translations.literal: ’ At that time Grand Commandant Jia Chong and Minister of Education Li Yin both died; the crown prince’s grand tutor was also vacant; Xu memorialized stating, ‘The three dukes as protectors and tutors ought to obtain the right men.’
translations.idiomatic: When Jia Chong and Li Yin died and the heir lacked a grand tutor, Xun Xu wrote: “The three elder statesmen who tutor the throne must be well chosen.”

sentences.zh: 若使楊珧參輔東宮，必當仰稱聖意。

translations.literal: If we cause Yang Yao to join in assisting the Eastern Palace, he will surely rise to match the sage intent.
translations.idiomatic: If Yang Yao assists the Eastern Palace, he will satisfy your aims.

sentences.zh: 尚書令衛瓘、吏部尚書山濤皆可為司徒。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Wei Guan and Minister of Personnel Shan Tao both can be Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Either Wei Guan, director of the secretariat, or Shan Tao, minister of personnel, can serve as minister of education.

sentences.zh: 若以瓘新為令未出者，濤即其人。

translations.literal: If because Guan is newly made supervisor and has not gone out, Tao is that man.
translations.idiomatic: If Wei Guan cannot leave Luoyang because he is new as director, then Shan Tao is the man.

sentences.zh: 」帝並從之。

translations.literal: ’ The emperor followed all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted every recommendation.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，諸州郡大水，兗土尤甚。

translations.literal: The next year autumn, the various provinces and commanderies had great flood; Yan soil was especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn floods struck many provinces, worst in Yan.

sentences.zh: 勖陳宜立都水使者。

translations.literal: Xu stated it was fitting to establish a capital-water commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He urged creation of a commissioner for water control.

sentences.zh: 其後門下啟通事令史伊羨、趙咸為舍人，對掌文法。

translations.literal: Afterward the Gate Bureau proposed General Affairs clerks Yi Xian and Zhao Xian as gentlemen attendants, paired to manage legal procedure.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellery then nominated clerks Yi Xian and Zhao Xian as attendants to oversee legal paperwork in pairs.

sentences.zh: 詔以問勖，勖曰：今天下幸賴陛下聖德，六合為一，望道化隆洽，垂之將來。

translations.literal: An edict used this to ask Xu; Xu said: ‘Now the realm fortunately relies on Your Majesty’s sagely virtue; the six directions are one; we hope the way’s transformation rises and harmonizes, hanging down to the future.’
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted him. Xun Xu replied: “Under your sage rule the realm is united; we look to moral influence that will last for generations.”

sentences.zh: 而門下上稱程咸、張惲，下稱此等，欲以文法為政，皆愚臣所未達者。

translations.literal: Yet the Gate Bureau above names Cheng Xian and Zhang Yun, below names these sorts, wishing to take legal procedure as governance—all what this foolish minister has not grasped.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Chancellery cites Cheng Xian and Zhang Yun and would run government by legal minutiae—something I cannot endorse.”

sentences.zh: 昔張釋之諫漢文，謂獸圈嗇夫不宜見用；

translations.literal: Formerly Zhang Shizhi remonstrated Han Wen, saying the animal-park clerk ought not be employed;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shizhi warned Han Wendi not to promote a mere park keeper;

sentences.zh: 邴吉住車，明調和陰陽之本。

translations.literal: Bing Ji stopped his cart, clarifying harmonizing yin and yang’s root.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Ji halted his carriage to teach that balancing yin and yang comes first;

sentences.zh: 此二人豈不知小吏之惠，誠重惜大化也。

translations.literal: Did these two men not know petty clerks’ convenience? Truly they valued and cherished great transformation.
translations.idiomatic: those men were not blind to petty convenience—they guarded the larger civilizing task.”

sentences.zh: 昔魏武帝使中軍司荀攸典刑獄，明帝時猶以付內常侍。

translations.literal: Formerly Wei Emperor Wu ordered Central Army Director Xun You to manage punishments and prisons; in Emperor Ming’s time still handed them to inner regular attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao once put Xun You in charge of penal affairs; Mingdi still entrusted such work to inner eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 以臣所聞，明帝時唯有通事劉泰等官，不過與殿中同號耳。

translations.literal: By what your servant has heard, in Emperor Ming’s time there were only General Affairs officials like Liu Tai and others, no more than sharing titles with palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingdi’s day there were only general-affairs posts like Liu Tai’s—titles much like palace clerks.

sentences.zh: 又頃言論者皆云省官減事，而求益吏者相尋矣。

translations.literal: Also recently debaters all say reduce officials and cut tasks, yet those seeking to increase clerks follow one another.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone talks of cutting offices, yet requests for more clerks never stop.

sentences.zh: 多云尚書郎太令史不親文書，乃委付書令史及幹，誠吏多則相倚也。

translations.literal: Many say Masters of Writing gentlemen and senior clerks do not personally handle documents, therefore delegate to document clerks and assistants—truly when clerks are many they lean on each other.
translations.idiomatic: They say secretariat gentlemen leave paperwork to subclerks and aides—piling on clerks only breeds mutual slack.

sentences.zh: 增置文法之職，適恐更耗擾台閣，臣竊謂不可。」

translations.literal: Adding legal-procedure posts will surely further waste and disturb the terrace pavilions; your servant privately says it cannot be done.’
translations.idiomatic: Adding legal specialists would only burden the ministries—I oppose it.”

sentences.zh: 時帝素知太子闇弱，恐後亂國，遣勖及和嶠往觀之。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor by nature knew the crown prince was dim and weak, feared he would later disorder the state, sent Xu and He Qiao to go observe him.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the heir was dull, the emperor sent Xun Xu and He Qiao to assess him.

sentences.zh: 勖還盛稱太子之德，而嶠云太子如初。

translations.literal: Xu returned greatly praising the crown prince’s virtue, but Qiao said the crown prince was as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu lavishly praised the prince; He Qiao reported that he was unchanged—still unfit.

sentences.zh: 於是天下貴嶠而賤勖。

translations.literal: Thereupon the realm honored Qiao and despised Xu.
translations.idiomatic: The world respected He Qiao and scorned Xun Xu.

sentences.zh: 帝將廢賈妃，勖與馮紞等諫請，故得不廢。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to depose Consort Jia; Xu with Feng Dan and others remonstrated and requested, therefore obtained not being deposed.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor considered deposing Empress Jia, Xun Xu and Feng Dan dissuaded him.

sentences.zh: 時議以勖傾國害時，孫資、劉放之匹。

translations.literal: At the time discussion held Xu overturned the state and harmed the age—a match for Sun Zi and Liu Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Critics ranked him with Sun Zi and Liu Fang as men who had ruined a dynasty.

sentences.zh: 然性慎密，每有詔令大事，雖已宣佈，然終不言，不欲使人知己豫聞也。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was cautious and secretive; whenever there were edict orders on great matters, though already proclaimed, in the end he did not speak, not wishing to cause people to know he had foreheard.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was tight-lipped: even after major edicts were issued he never hinted that he had known beforehand.

sentences.zh: 族弟良曾勸勖曰：「公大失物情，有所進益者自可語之，則懷恩多矣。

translations.literal: Clan younger brother Liang once urged Xu saying, ‘The lord greatly loses creatures’ feelings; those who have advancement benefit—you may tell them, then many will harbor gratitude.’
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Xun Liang urged him to share news with allies so they would feel obliged.

sentences.zh: 」其婿武統亦說勖「宜有所營置，令有歸戴者」。

translations.literal: ’ His son-in-law Wu Tong also urged Xu ‘ought to have some establishment, causing there to be those who return allegiance.’
translations.idiomatic: His son-in-law Wu Tong likewise told him to build a client network.

sentences.zh: 勖並默然不應，退而語諸子曰：「人臣不密則失身，樹私則背公，是大戒也。

translations.literal: Xu together was silent and did not respond; retiring spoke to the various sons saying, ‘A minister not secret then loses his person; planting private then turns from the public—this is the great warning.’
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu stayed silent and later told his sons: “Loose talk ruins a minister; private factions betray the public—that is my rule.”

sentences.zh: 汝等亦當宦達人間，宜識吾此意。

translations.literal: You also will someday serve in office among men; ought to know my this intent.
translations.idiomatic: When you serve in the world, remember this.”

sentences.zh: 」久之，以勖守尚書令。

translations.literal: ’ After long time, Xu was made acting Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he was named acting director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 勖久在中書，專管機事。

translations.literal: Xu long was in the Palace Secretariat, solely managing secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He had long run the secretariat and its confidential business.

sentences.zh: 及失之，甚罔罔悵恨。

translations.literal: When he lost it, very dazed and regretful.
translations.idiomatic: Losing that post left him despondent.

sentences.zh: 或有賀之者，勖曰：「奪我鳳皇池，諸君賀我邪！

translations.literal: Some congratulated him; Xu said, ‘You seize my phoenix pool—gentlemen, you congratulate me?’
translations.idiomatic: When people congratulated him on his new job, he snapped, “You have stolen my Phoenix Pool—why congratulate me?”

sentences.zh: 」及在尚書，課試令史以下，核其才能，有暗于文法，不能決疑處事者，即時遣出。

translations.literal: ’ When at the Masters of Writing, he examined clerks downward, examining their talent and ability; those dark in legal procedure, unable to decide doubt and handle affairs, immediately sent out.
translations.idiomatic: At the Ministry of Personnel he tested junior clerks and expelled anyone who could not master statutes or settle cases.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗謂曰：「魏武帝言'荀文若之進善，不進不止；

translations.literal: The emperor once said to him, ‘Wei Emperor Wu said, “Xun Wenruo’s advancing good, not advancing then not stopping;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor quoted Cao Cao: “As Xun Yu promoted good, he never stopped pushing good;

sentences.zh: 荀公達之退惡，不退不休'。

translations.literal: Xun Gongda’s retiring evil, not retiring then not ceasing.”’
translations.idiomatic: as Xun You curbed evil, he never stopped rooting it out.”

sentences.zh: 二令君之美，亦望於君也。

translations.literal: The two directors’ excellence is also hoped from you.
translations.idiomatic: I expect the same excellence from you.”

sentences.zh: 」居職月餘，以母憂上還印綬，帝不許。

translations.literal: ’ Holding office over a month, by mother’s mourning he upward returned seals and ribbons; the emperor did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: After a month his mother died; he tried to resign, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 遣常侍周恢喻旨，勖乃奉詔視職。

translations.literal: He sent Regular Attendant Zhou Hui to convey intent; Xu then received edict and took office.
translations.idiomatic: Regular attendant Zhou Hui conveyed the imperial will, and he returned to duty.

sentences.zh: 勖久管機密，有才思，探得人主微旨，不犯顏忤爭，故得始終全其寵祿。

translations.literal: Xu long managed secrets, had talent and thought, probed the ruler’s subtle intent, did not offend countenance or contradict in dispute, therefore obtained from beginning to end preserving his favor and salary.
translations.idiomatic: He long handled secrets, read the ruler’s wishes, and never argued face to face, which preserved his favor to the end.

sentences.zh: 卒，詔贈司徒，賜東園秘器、朝服一具、錢五十萬、布百匹。

translations.literal: He died; edict posthumously gifted Minister of Education, bestowed Eastern Garden secret goods, one set court dress, five hundred thousand cash, one hundred bolts cloth.
translations.idiomatic: On his death he was posthumously named minister of education, with Eastern Garden coffin fittings, court robes, five hundred thousand cash, and a hundred bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 遣兼御史持節護喪，諡曰成。

translations.literal: Sent concurrent censor credential bearer to protect the funeral; posthumous name Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: A censor escorted the funeral, and his posthumous title was Cheng (“Accomplished”).

sentences.zh: 勖有十子，其達者輯、藩、組。

translations.literal: Xu had ten sons; those who rose were Ji, Fan, and Zu.
translations.idiomatic: Of his ten sons, Ji, Fan, and Zu became prominent.

sentences.zh: 輯嗣，官至衛尉。

translations.literal: Ji succeeded; office reached Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Ji inherited the title and rose to commandant of the guards.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous name Jian.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Jian.

sentences.zh: 子畯嗣。

translations.literal: Son Jun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun Jun succeeded.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰烈。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous name Lie.
translations.idiomatic: He received the posthumous name Lie.

sentences.zh: 無嫡子，以弟息識為嗣。

translations.literal: Having no legitimate son, took younger brother’s son Shi as successor.
translations.idiomatic: Without a legitimate heir, he named his nephew Xun Shi as successor.

sentences.zh: 輯子綽。

translations.literal: Ji’s son Chuo.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson was Xun Chuo.

sentences.zh: 綽字彥舒，博學有才能，撰《晉後書》十五篇，傳於世。

translations.literal: Chuo, courtesy name Yanshu, broadly learned with talent and ability, compiled *Later Jin History* in fifteen sections, transmitted in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Chuo, courtesy name Yanshu, wrote the fifteen-chapter *Jin hou shu*.

sentences.zh: 永嘉末，為司空從事中郎，沒于石勒，為勒參軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongjia, he was Minister of Works attendant clerk, lost to Shi Le, became Le’s staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yongjia he served on the staff of the minister of works, fell into Shi Le’s hands, and became his aide.

translations.literal: The text reads '='.
translations.idiomatic: Table marker equals sign in the received text.

sentences.zh: 子藩

translations.literal: Son: Fan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun Fan.

sentences.zh: =藩字大堅。

translations.literal: Table line: Fan, courtesy name Dajian.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Fan, courtesy name Dajian (genealogical table entry).

sentences.zh: 元康中，為黃門侍郎，受詔成父所治鐘磬。

translations.literal: In the Yuankang years, he was Yellow Gate Gentleman, received edict to complete bells and stones his father had regulated.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuankang he was a yellow-gate gentleman and finished his father’s musical project on the bells.

sentences.zh: 以從駕討齊王冏勳，封西華縣公。

translations.literal: By merit in accompanying the campaign against Prince of Qi Jiong, enfeoffed Duke of Xihua county.
translations.idiomatic: He earned the county duchy of Xihua for joining the expedition against Sima Jiong.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書令。

translations.literal: Promoted in stages to Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 永嘉末，轉司空，未拜而洛陽陷沒，藩出奔密。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongjia, transferred to Minister of Works; before investiture Luoyang fell and sank; Fan fled out to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yongjia he was named minister of works, but before he could take office Luoyang fell; he fled to Mi.

sentences.zh: 王浚承制，奉藩為留台太尉。

translations.literal: Wang Jun held the mandate and installed Fan as caretaker grand commandant at the provisional court.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun, acting on his own authority, made him grand commandant of the exiled court.

sentences.zh: 及愍帝為太子，委藩督攝遠近。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min was crown prince, he entrusted Fan to supervise near and far.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min was heir, he put Xun Fan in charge of coordinating loyalist forces.

sentences.zh: 薨於開封，年六十九，因葬亡所。

translations.literal: He died at Kaifeng, age sixty-nine, and was buried where he fell.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kaifeng at sixty-nine and was buried on the spot.

sentences.zh: 諡曰成，追贈太保。

translations.literal: Posthumous name Cheng; posthumously gifted Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Cheng; he was later honored as grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 藩二子：邃、闓。

translations.literal: Fan had two sons: Sui and Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Fan’s sons were Xun Sui and Xun Kai.

translations.literal: The text reads '=='.
translations.idiomatic: Double equals table marker in the received text.

sentences.zh: 藩子邃、闓

translations.literal: Fan’s sons: Sui and Kai.
translations.idiomatic: The sons of Xun Fan: Xun Sui and Xun Kai.

sentences.zh: 邃字道玄，解音樂，善談論。

translations.literal: Sui, courtesy name Daoxuan, understood music, good at discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Sui, courtesy name Daoxuan, knew music and was a fine conversationalist.

sentences.zh: 弱冠辟趙王倫相國掾，遷太子洗馬。

translations.literal: At weak cap summoned as Prince of Zhao Lun’s chancellor clerk, promoted to crown prince attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he joined Sima Lun’s staff and became attendant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 長沙王乂以為參軍。

translations.literal: Prince of Changsha Yi made him staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi of Changsha made him an aide.

sentences.zh: 乂敗，成都王為皇太弟，精選僚屬，以邃為中舍人。

translations.literal: When Yi was defeated, Prince of Chengdu was imperial younger brother, finely selected subordinates, making Sui central gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Yi fell, Sima Ying as imperial younger brother chose him as palace gentleman.

sentences.zh: 鄴城不守，隨藩在密。

translations.literal: Ye city did not hold; he followed Fan in Mi.
translations.idiomatic: When Ye fell he joined his father in Mi.

sentences.zh: 元帝召為丞相從事中郎，以道險不就。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan summoned him as attendant clerk to the chancellor; because the road was dangerous he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan offered him a post on the chancellor’s staff, but the journey was too perilous.

sentences.zh: 愍帝就加左將軍、陳留相。

translations.literal: Emperor Min additionally appointed General of the Left and administrator of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min later named him general of the left and administrator of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 父憂去職，服闋，襲封。

translations.literal: Father mourning removed him from office; when mourning ended, he inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned for his father’s mourning, then inherited the noble title.

sentences.zh: 愍帝欲納邃女，先徵為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Emperor Min wished to take Sui’s daughter; first summoned him as Regular Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted Sui’s daughter as consort and first summoned him as regular cavalier attendant.

sentences.zh: 邃懼西都危逼，故不應命，而東渡江，元帝以為軍諮祭酒。

translations.literal: Sui feared the western capital’s peril and pressure, therefore did not answer the summons, but crossed east the river; Emperor Yuan made him libationer for military counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the doomed western court, he ignored the summons, crossed south of the Yangzi, and became military adviser to Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 太興初，拜侍中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taixing, appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taixing he was palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 邃與刁協婚親，時協執權，欲以邃為吏部尚書，邃深距之。

translations.literal: Sui was marriage kin to Diao Xie; at the time Xie held power and wished to make Sui Minister of Personnel; Sui deeply refused.
translations.idiomatic: Related by marriage to Diao Xie, he firmly refused when Diao tried to make him minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 尋而王敦討協，協黨與並及於難，唯邃以疏協獲免。

translations.literal: Soon Wang Dun attacked Xie; Xie’s faction all met disaster; only Sui by keeping distant from Xie escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun moved against Diao Xie, the faction was ruined, but Xun Sui’s aloofness saved him.

sentences.zh: 敦表為廷尉，以疾不拜。

translations.literal: Dun memorialized him as commandant of justice; because of illness he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun nominated him as commandant of justice; illness kept him from accepting.

sentences.zh: 遷太常，轉尚書。

translations.literal: Promoted Grand Master of Ceremonies, transferred to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He became grand master of ceremonies, then minister.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻作亂，邃與王導、荀崧並侍天子于石頭。

translations.literal: When Su Jun rebelled, Sui with Wang Dao and Xun Song together attended the Son of Heaven at Stone Fort.
translations.idiomatic: During Su Jun’s revolt he stayed with the emperor at Shitou alongside Wang Dao and Xun Song.

sentences.zh: 峻平後卒，贈金紫光祿大夫，諡曰靖。

translations.literal: After Jun was pacified he died; posthumously gifted golden-purple Grand Master of Splendid Carriage; posthumous name Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died after Su Jun’s defeat and was honored as golden-purple grand master with the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 子汪嗣。

translations.literal: Son Wang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun Wang inherited.

sentences.zh: 闓字道明，亦有名稱，京都為之語曰：「洛中英英荀道明。

translations.literal: Kai, courtesy name Daoming, also had reputation; the capital for them made a saying, ‘In Luoyang, bright bright Xun Daoming.’
translations.idiomatic: Xun Kai, courtesy name Daoming, was famous; Luoyang sang, “Splendid in Luoyang—Xun Daoming.”

sentences.zh: 」大司馬、齊王冏辟為掾。

translations.literal: ’ Grand Marshal, Prince of Qi Jiong summoned him as clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Grand marshal Sima Jiong took him as clerk.

sentences.zh: 冏敗，暴屍已三日，莫敢收葬。

translations.literal: When Jiong was defeated, exposed corpse already three days, none dared collect and bury.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiong’s defeat his corpse lay in the square three days untended.

sentences.zh: 闓與冏故吏李述、嵇含等露板請葬，朝議聽之，論者稱焉。

translations.literal: Kai with Jiong’s former clerks Li Shu, Ji Han and others exposed boards requesting burial; court discussion permitted it; debaters praised.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Kai, Li Shu, and Ji Han petitioned for burial; the court agreed, and people praised them.

sentences.zh: 為太傅主簿、中書郎。

translations.literal: He was Grand Tutor chief clerk, Palace Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief clerk to the grand tutor and palace gentleman.

sentences.zh: 與邃俱渡江，拜丞相軍諮祭酒。

translations.literal: Together with Sui crossed the river, appointed libationer for the chancellor’s military counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yangzi with his brother and became the chancellor’s military adviser.

sentences.zh: 中興建，遷右軍將軍，轉少府。

translations.literal: When the Restoration was established, promoted General of the Right Army, transferred to Minister of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration he became general of the right army, then minister of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 明帝嘗從容問王暠曰：「二荀兄弟孰賢？

translations.literal: Emperor Ming once casually asked Wang Gao saying, ‘Of the two Xun brothers, which is worthy?’
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming once asked Wang Gao which Xun brother was the better man.

sentences.zh: 」暠答以闓才明過邃。

translations.literal: ’ Gao answered that Kai’s talent and clarity surpassed Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gao said Xun Kai was cleverer.

sentences.zh: 帝以語庾亮，亮曰：「邃真粹之地，亦闓所不及。

translations.literal: The emperor used this to tell Yu Liang; Liang said, ‘Sui’s true pure ground is also what Kai does not reach.’
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang replied that Xun Sui’s integrity was beyond Xun Kai.

sentences.zh: 」由是議者莫能定其兄弟優劣。

translations.literal: ’ Thereby debaters none could fix their brothers’ superiority or inferiority.
translations.idiomatic: Critics never settled which brother was greater.

sentences.zh: 歷御史中丞、侍中、尚書，封射陽公。

translations.literal: He passed through Palace Assistant Clerk, Palace Attendant, Minister, enfeoffed Duke of Sheyang.
translations.idiomatic: He held palace assistant clerk, palace attendant, and minister, and was duke of Sheyang.

sentences.zh: 卒，追贈衛尉，諡曰定。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously gifted Commandant of the Guards; posthumous name Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was named commandant of the guards with the title Ding.

sentences.zh: 子達嗣。

translations.literal: Son Da succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun Da inherited.

sentences.zh: =藩弟組=

translations.literal: Table line: Fan’s younger brother Zu.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Zu, younger brother of Xun Fan (genealogical table entry).

sentences.zh: 組字大章。

translations.literal: Zu, courtesy name Dazhang.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Zu, courtesy name Dazhang.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，太尉王衍見而稱之曰：「夷雅有才識。

translations.literal: At weak cap, Grand Commandant Wang Yan saw him and praised him saying, ‘Calm and elegant, with talent and judgment.’
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he impressed Grand Commandant Wang Yan, who called him refined, capable, and astute.

sentences.zh: 」初為司徒左西屬，補太子舍人。

translations.literal: ’ At first he was Western Subordinate of the Minister of Education’s left wing, supplemented as crown prince gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He began as an aide on the minister of education’s staff, then became a gentleman of the heir’s household.

sentences.zh: 司徒王渾請為從事中郎，轉左長史，歷太子中庶子、滎陽太守。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Wang Hun requested him as attendant clerk, transferred to left chief clerk, passed through crown prince palace aide and administrator of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun took him as staff aide; he rose to left chief clerk, then palace aide to the crown prince, then governor of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫為相國，欲收大名，選海內德望之士，以江夏李重及組為左右長史，東平王堪、沛國劉謨為左右司馬。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Lun was chancellor, wishing to gather great fame, selected men of virtue and reputation within the seas, making Jiangxia Li Chong and Zu left and right chief clerks, Dongping Wang Kan and Pei Liu Mo left and right majors.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Lun was chancellor he recruited eminent men, naming Li Chong of Jiangxia and Xun Zu as his chief clerks and Wang Kan of Dongping and Liu Mo of Pei as his majors.

sentences.zh: 倫篡，以組為侍中。

translations.literal: When Lun usurped, he made Zu Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Lun seized the throne, Xun Zu became palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 及長沙王乂敗，惠帝遣組及散騎常侍閭丘沖詣成都王穎，慰勞其軍。

translations.literal: When Prince of Changsha Yi was defeated, Emperor Hui sent Zu and Regular Cavalier Attendant Lüqiu Chong to go to Prince of Chengdu Ying, comforting and laboring his army.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Yi of Changsha fell, Emperor Hui sent Xun Zu and Lüqiu Chong to console Sima Ying’s army.

sentences.zh: 帝西幸長安，以組為河南尹。

translations.literal: The emperor went west in fortune to Chang’an, making Zu Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When the court fled to Chang’an, Xun Zu was named governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書，轉衛尉，賜爵成陽縣男，加散騎常侍、中書監。

translations.literal: Promoted Minister, transferred Commandant of the Guards, granted noble rank Baron of Chengyang, added Regular Cavalier Attendant, Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He became minister, then commandant of the guards, baron of Chengyang, and added posts as cavalier attendant and secretariat director.

sentences.zh: 轉司隸校尉，加特進、光祿大夫，常侍如故。

translations.literal: Transferred Metropolitan Commandant, added specially advanced, Grand Master of Splendid Carriage, regular attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was metropolitan commandant with the honorific “specially advanced” and grand master of splendid carriage, keeping his cavalier attendant post.

sentences.zh: 于時天下已亂，組兄弟貴盛，懼不容於世，雖居大官，並諷議而已。

translations.literal: At that time all under heaven was already in chaos; Zu’s brothers were noble and flourishing; they feared not being tolerated in the age; though holding great offices, they only offered indirect remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: As the realm collapsed, the Xun brothers feared for their lives; though they held high rank, they offered only muted advice.

sentences.zh: 永嘉末，復以組為侍中，領太子太保。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongjia, again made Zu Palace Attendant, concurrent Grand Guardian to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yongjia he was again palace attendant and grand guardian to the heir.

sentences.zh: 未拜，會劉曜、王彌逼洛陽，組與藩俱出奔。

translations.literal: Before investiture, it happened Liu Yao and Wang Mi pressed Luoyang; Zu together with Fan both fled out.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take office, Liu Yao and Wang Mi threatened Luoyang; he fled with Xun Fan.

sentences.zh: 懷帝蒙塵，司空王浚以組為司隸校尉。

translations.literal: Emperor Huai suffered dust; Minister of Works Wang Jun made Zu Metropolitan Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Huai’s ordeal, Wang Jun named him metropolitan commandant.

sentences.zh: 組與藩移檄天下，以琅邪王為盟主。

translations.literal: Zu together with Fan moved proclamations through all under heaven, making Prince of Langye the covenant lord.
translations.idiomatic: He and Xun Fan issued a manifesto making the prince of Langye, Sima Rui, leader of the loyalist league.

sentences.zh: 愍帝稱皇太子，組即太子之舅，又領司隸校尉，行豫州刺史事，與藩並保滎陽之開封。

translations.literal: Emperor Min was styled crown prince; Zu was the crown prince’s maternal uncle; also held Metropolitan Commandant, acting Inspector of Yu Province, together with Fan both guarding Kaifeng in Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min was heir apparent, Xun Zu as his uncle served as metropolitan commandant and acting inspector of Yu, holding Kaifeng with Xun Fan.

sentences.zh: 建興初，詔藩行留台事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianxing, edict ordered Fan to act caretaker court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianxing, Xun Fan was put in charge of the exiled court.

sentences.zh: 俄而藩薨，帝更以組為司空，領尚書左僕射，又兼司隸，復行留台事，州征郡守皆承制行焉。

translations.literal: Soon Fan died; the emperor changed to making Zu Minister of Works, holding Vice Director of the Masters of Writing left, also concurrent Metropolitan Commandant, again acting caretaker court; provincial inspectors and commandery governors all acted on his orders.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun Fan died, Xun Zu became minister of works, vice director of the secretariat, and again metropolitan commandant and head of the provisional government, with regional officials obeying his writs.

sentences.zh: 進封臨潁縣公，加太夫人、世子印綬。

translations.literal: Advanced enfeoffment to Duke of Linying county, added seals for the grand lady and heir.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to duke of Linying and his mother and heir received formal seals.

sentences.zh: 明年，進位太尉，領豫州牧、假節。

translations.literal: The next year, advanced in rank to Grand Commandant, holding Shepherd of Yu Province, credential staff.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became grand commandant, governor of Yu, with the imperial baton.

sentences.zh: 元帝承制，以組都督司州諸軍，加散騎常侍，餘如故。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan held the mandate, making Zu area commander of all Si Province armies, added Regular Cavalier Attendant, remainder as before.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Rui authorized him as commander of Si province forces with added cavalier attendant rank.

sentences.zh: 頃之，又除尚書令，表讓不拜。

translations.literal: Shortly, again removed as Supervisor of the Masters of Writing; he memorialized decline and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He was named director of the secretariat but declined.

sentences.zh: 及西都不守，組乃遣使移檄天下共勸進。

translations.literal: When the western capital did not hold, Zu then sent envoys moving proclamations through all under heaven jointly urging advance to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang’an fell, he sent circulars urging Sima Rui to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝欲以組為司徒，以問太常賀循。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to make Zu Minister of Education; used this to ask Grand Master of Ceremonies He Xun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked He Xun whether Xun Zu should be minister of education.

sentences.zh: 循曰：「組舊望清重，忠勤顯著，遷訓五品，實允眾望。

translations.literal: Xun said, ‘Zu’s old reputation is clear and weighty; loyal diligence is manifest; promotion through the five grades truly fits the multitude’s hope.’
translations.idiomatic: He Xun replied that Xun Zu’s prestige and loyal service made him the obvious choice for the ministry of education.

sentences.zh: 」於是拜組為司徒。

translations.literal: ’ Thereupon Zu was appointed Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Zu was appointed minister of education.

sentences.zh: 組逼于石勒，不能自立。

translations.literal: Zu was pressed by Shi Le and could not stand on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Hemmed in by Shi Le, he could not hold his ground.

sentences.zh: 太興初，自許昌率其屬數百人渡江，給千兵百騎，組先所領仍皆統攝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taixing, from Xuchang he led his subordinates several hundred men crossing the river; given one thousand infantry and one hundred cavalry; what Zu earlier led still all commanded.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taixing he brought several hundred followers from Xuchang across the Yangzi; the court gave him a thousand foot and a hundred horse and let him keep his old command.

sentences.zh: 頃之，詔組與太保、西陽王羕並錄尚書事，各加班劍六十人。

translations.literal: Shortly, edict ordered Zu together with Grand Guardian, Prince of Xiyang Yi jointly to record Masters of Writing affairs, each given sixty ceremonial sword guards.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to share secretariat duties with Sima Yi, prince of Xiyang, each with sixty guards bearing honor swords.

sentences.zh: 永昌初，遷太尉，領太子太保。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongchang, promoted Grand Commandant, concurrent Grand Guardian to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchang he was named grand commandant and grand guardian to the heir.

sentences.zh: 未拜，薨，年六十五。

translations.literal: Before investiture, he died, age sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died before taking office, at sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 諡曰元。

translations.literal: Posthumous name Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Yuan.

sentences.zh: 子奕嗣。

translations.literal: Son Yi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun Yi inherited.

sentences.zh: 組子奕

translations.literal: Zu's son Yi
translations.idiomatic: The son of Xun Zu: Xun Yi.

sentences.zh: 奕字玄欣。

translations.literal: Yi, courtesy name Xuanxin.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yi, courtesy name Xuanxin.

sentences.zh: 少拜太子舍人、駙馬都尉，侍講東宮。

translations.literal: In youth appointed crown prince gentleman, Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law, lecturing in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Young, he was gentleman to the heir, commandant of the imperial son-in-law’s escort, and lecturer in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 出為鎮東參軍，行揚武將軍、新汲令。

translations.literal: Went out as staff officer to the east, acting General Who Displays Might, magistrate of Xinji.
translations.idiomatic: He served on the eastern headquarters staff as acting General Who Displays Might and magistrate of Xinji.

sentences.zh: 愍帝為皇太子，召為中舍人，尋拜散騎侍郎，皆不就。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min was crown prince, summoned as central gentleman; soon appointed Regular Cavalier Gentleman; all did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min was heir, he was summoned as palace gentleman and then cavalier gentleman, but refused both posts.

sentences.zh: 隨父渡江。

translations.literal: Followed father crossing the river.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed south with his father.

sentences.zh: 元帝踐阼，拜中庶子，遷給事黃門郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan ascended the throne, appointed palace aide, promoted to Supervising Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Rui took the throne he became palace aide, then supervising gentleman of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 父憂去職，服闋，補散騎常侍、侍中。

translations.literal: Father mourning removed him from office; when mourning ended, supplemented Regular Cavalier Attendant, Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned for his father’s death, then returned as cavalier attendant and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 時將繕宮城，尚書符下陳留王，使出城夫。

translations.literal: At the time about to repair the palace city, the Masters of Writing issued a tally to Prince of Chenliu, ordering him to supply corvée laborers.
translations.idiomatic: When the palace was to be rebuilt, the ministry ordered the prince of Chenliu to furnish laborers.

sentences.zh: 奕駁曰：「昔虞賓在位，《書》稱其美；

translations.literal: Yi refuted saying, ‘Formerly the Yu guest held position; the *Documents* praises his beauty;’
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yi objected: “The *Shang shu* praises the Shang who honored the guest-king Yu;

sentences.zh: 《詩》詠《有客》，載在《雅》《頌》。

translations.literal: the *Odes* chant *You ke*, recorded in *Ya* and *Song*.
translations.idiomatic: the *Book of Odes* celebrates the guest in pieces preserved in the *Ya* and *Song*.”

sentences.zh: 今陳留王位在三公之上，坐在太子右，故答表曰書，賜物曰與。

translations.literal: Now Prince of Chenliu’s rank is above the three dukes; his seat is to the crown prince’s right; therefore answering memorials says ‘letter,’ bestowing goods says ‘give.’
translations.idiomatic: Today the prince of Chenliu ranks above the three dukes and sits to the heir’s right; he receives letters and gifts in special forms.

sentences.zh: 此古今之所崇，體國之高義也。

translations.literal: This is what antiquity honors and the high righteousness of ordering the state.
translations.idiomatic: That is the dignity the state owes him.

sentences.zh: 謂宜除夫役。

translations.literal: I say it is fitting to remove corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: He should be excused from corvée.

sentences.zh: 」時尚書張闓、僕射孔愉難奕，以為：「昔宋不城周，《陽秋》所譏。

translations.literal: ’ At the time Minister Zhang Kai and Vice Director Kong Yu challenged Yi, holding, ‘Formerly Song did not wall Zhou—what *Yangqiu* ridicules. Special exemption from the norm ought to mean reducing laborers.’
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kai and Kong Yu countered that *Chunqiu* mocked Song for refusing to wall Zhou for the Zhou king, and that exemptions should still mean fewer laborers.

sentences.zh: 特蠲非體，宜應減夫。

translations.literal: Special exemption from the usual rule should still mean reducing the labor quota.’
translations.idiomatic: They argued that even a special exemption ought to trim the corvée, not cancel it entirely.’

sentences.zh: 」奕重駁，以為：「《陽秋》之末，文武之道將墜於地，新有子朝之亂，于時諸侯逋替，莫肯率職。

translations.literal: Yi again refuted, holding, ‘At the end of *Yangqiu*, the way of Wen and Wu was about to fall to earth; newly there was Zichao’s chaos; at that time the lords shirked duty, none willing to perform office.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yi replied that in the late *Chunqiu* age lords had abandoned their duties amid Zichao’s turmoil,

sentences.zh: 宋之于周，實有列國之權。

translations.literal: Song toward Zhou truly had the power of a ranked state.
translations.idiomatic: and Song toward Zhou had been a peer polity with real leverage,

sentences.zh: 且同巳勤王而主之者晉，客而辭役，責之可也。

translations.literal: and moreover the same had aided the royal house while Jin was host; as guest declining corvée, blame could apply.
translations.idiomatic: so refusing labor then was a different matter from today.

sentences.zh: 今之陳留，無列國之勢，此之作否，何益有無！

translations.literal: Now Chenliu has no power of a ranked state; whether this is done or not, what benefit or harm is there!
translations.idiomatic: The prince of Chenliu is no feudal rival; exempting him hurts nothing and gains the state’s honor.

sentences.zh: 臣以為宜除，于國職為全。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks it fitting to remove; for the state’s duty it is complete.
translations.idiomatic: He urged full exemption as proper policy.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: ’ Edict followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 時又通議元會日帝應敬司徒王導不。

translations.literal: At the time again jointly debated whether on the new year court day the emperor should show respect to Minister of Education Wang Dao.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated whether the emperor should bow to Wang Dao at the new-year audience.

sentences.zh: 博士郭熙、杜援等以為禮無拜臣之文，謂宜除敬。

translations.literal: Erudites Guo Xi, Du Yuan and others held ritual has no text of bowing to ministers; said it was fitting to remove respect.
translations.idiomatic: Doctors Guo Xi and Du Yuan said rites never required the sovereign to bow to a subject.

sentences.zh: 侍中馮懷議曰：「天子修禮，莫盛於辟雍。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Feng Huai argued saying, ‘The Son of Heaven cultivating ritual, nothing greater than the suburban school.’
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant Feng Huai countered that the emperor’s highest ritual was the lecture hall at the moat school.

sentences.zh: 當爾之日，猶拜三老，況今先帝師傅。

translations.literal: When that day came, still bowed to the three elders; how much more the former emperor’s tutor and protector.
translations.idiomatic: On that occasion the ruler still bowed to the three elders—how much more should he honor his late father’s tutor.

sentences.zh: 謂宜盡敬。

translations.literal: Said it was fitting to show full respect.
translations.idiomatic: He favored the emperor showing full deference.

sentences.zh: 」事下門下，奕議曰：「三朝之首，宜明君臣之體，則不應敬。

translations.literal: ’ The matter went down to the Gate Bureau; Yi argued saying, ‘On the first of the three great audiences, it is fitting to clarify lord-minister body; then one should not show respect.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yi held that at the grand new-year levee the ruler-subject distinction must be clear, so no bow was proper,

sentences.zh: 若他日小會，自可盡禮。

translations.literal: If on other days at small gatherings, naturally full ritual may be used.
translations.idiomatic: while smaller meetings could allow personal courtesies.

sentences.zh: 又至尊與公書手詔則曰'頓首言'，中書為詔則云'敬問'，散騎優冊則曰：'制命'。

translations.literal: Moreover the supreme and the duke in handwritten edicts say “bow head and speak,” the Central Secretariat in edicts says “respectful inquiry,” the Cavalier’s edict of investiture says “ordered by mandate.”
translations.idiomatic: Imperial notes to Wang Dao used humble phrasing unlike ordinary edicts,

sentences.zh: 今詔文尚異，況大會之與小會，理豈得同！

translations.literal: Now edict texts still differ; how much more great assembly versus small assembly—how can principle be the same!
translations.idiomatic: so grand audiences and private audiences could not follow one rule.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: ’ Edict followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted Xun Yi’s view.

sentences.zh: 卒，追贈太僕，諡曰定。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously gifted Grand Coachman; posthumous name Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was grand coachman with the title Ding.

sentences.zh: 馮紞

translations.literal: Feng Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Feng Dan.

sentences.zh: 馮紞，字少胄，安平人也。

translations.literal: Feng Dan, courtesy name Shaozhou, a man of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dan, courtesy name Shaozhou, came from Anping.

sentences.zh: 祖浮，魏司隸校尉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fu was Wei Metropolitan Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Feng Fu had been Wei metropolitan commandant.

sentences.zh: 父員，汲郡太守。

translations.literal: His father Yuan was Administrator of Ji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Feng Yuan was governor of Ji commandery.

sentences.zh: 紞少博涉經史，識悟機辯。

translations.literal: Dan in youth broadly traversed classics and histories, with keen insight and quick debate.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in the classics and histories and was sharp in debate.

sentences.zh: 歷仕為魏郡太守，轉步兵校尉，徙越騎。

translations.literal: He served as Administrator of Wei commandery, transferred Colonel of Foot Soldiers, moved to Colonel of the Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Wei commandery, then commanded the foot-soldier and agile-cavalry guards.

sentences.zh: 得幸于武帝，稍遷左衛將軍。

translations.literal: He obtained favor from Emperor Wu, gradually promoted General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Favored by Sima Yan, he rose to general of the left guard.

sentences.zh: 承顏悅色，寵愛日隆。

translations.literal: He bore pleasing countenance and daily grew in love.
translations.idiomatic: He flattered the emperor and grew ever more favored.

sentences.zh: 賈充、荀勖並與之親善。

translations.literal: Jia Chong and Xun Xu were both intimate and good with him.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong and Xun Xu were his allies.

sentences.zh: 充女之為皇太子妃也，紞有力焉。

translations.literal: When Chong’s daughter became the crown prince’s consort, Dan had strength therein.
translations.idiomatic: He helped make Jia Chong’s daughter crown princess.

sentences.zh: 及妃之將廢，紞、勖幹沒救請，故得不廢。

translations.literal: When the consort was about to be deposed, Dan and Xu interfered and pleaded; therefore obtained not being deposed.
translations.idiomatic: When she faced deposition, he and Xun Xu intervened to save her.

sentences.zh: 伐吳之役，紞領汝南太守，以郡兵隨王浚入秣陵。

translations.literal: In the campaign attacking Wu, Dan held Administrator of Runan, with commandery troops following Wang Jun into Moling.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wu conquest he led Runan troops with Wang Jun into Moling.

sentences.zh: 遷御史中丞，轉侍中。

translations.literal: Promoted Palace Assistant Clerk, transferred Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He became palace assistant clerk, then palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 帝病篤得愈，紞與勖見朝野之望，屬在齊王攸。

translations.literal: When the emperor gravely ill recovered, Dan and Xu saw court and countryside’s hope rested in Prince of Qi You.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Yan’s recovery, he and Xun Xu saw the realm looking to Sima You.

sentences.zh: 攸素薄勖。

translations.literal: You by nature slighted Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Sima You despised Xun Xu.

sentences.zh: 勖以太子愚劣，恐攸得立，有害於己，乃使紞言於帝曰：「陛下前者疾若不差，太子其廢矣。

translations.literal: Xu because the crown prince was foolish and inferior, feared You would obtain establishment, having harm to himself, therefore caused Dan to speak to the emperor saying, ‘Your Majesty’s former illness if it had not improved, the crown prince would have been deposed.’
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Sima You would replace the feeble heir and ruin their faction, Xun Xu had Feng Dan warn that Sima You would have taken the throne had the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 齊王為百姓所歸，公卿所仰，雖欲高讓，其得免乎！

translations.literal: Prince of Qi is what the hundred surnames return to, what dukes and ministers look up to; though wishing lofty yielding, can he obtain escape!
translations.idiomatic: The people and elite favored Sima You; he could not refuse the throne forever.

sentences.zh: 宜遣還藩，以安社稷。

translations.literal: It is fitting to send him back to his fief to secure the altars of soil and grain.’
translations.idiomatic: He should be sent to his princedom for the dynasty’s safety.”

sentences.zh: 」帝納之。

translations.literal: ’ The emperor accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 及攸薨，朝野悲恨。

translations.literal: When You died, court and countryside grieved and resented.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima You died, officials and commoners mourned bitterly.

sentences.zh: 初，帝友于之情甚篤，既納紞、勖邪說，遂為身後之慮，以固儲位。

translations.literal: At first the emperor’s friendship feeling was very thick; having accepted Dan and Xu’s crooked talk, then had anxiety for after death, to solidify the heir’s position.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan had loved his brother; after believing Feng Dan and Xun Xu, he secured the infirm heir at terrible cost.

sentences.zh: 既聞攸殞，哀慟特深。

translations.literal: Having heard You’s death, grief was especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of the death, he grieved intensely.

sentences.zh: 紞侍立，因言曰：「齊王名過於實，今得自終，此乃大晉之福。

translations.literal: Dan attending upright, then spoke saying, ‘Prince of Qi’s name exceeded the reality; now obtaining natural end—this is great Jin’s blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dan said Sima You’s fame outran his worth and his natural death was Jin’s good fortune,

sentences.zh: 陛下何乃過哀！

translations.literal: Your Majesty how then excessive grief!’
translations.idiomatic: and urged the emperor not to mourn excessively.

sentences.zh: 」帝收淚而止。

translations.literal: ’ The emperor gathered tears and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan checked his tears.

sentences.zh: 初謀伐吳，紞與賈充、荀勖同共苦諫不可。

translations.literal: At first planning to attack Wu, Dan together with Jia Chong, Xun Xu jointly bitterly remonstrated it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: He had fiercely opposed the Wu campaign alongside Jia Chong and Xun Xu.

sentences.zh: 吳平，紞內懷慚懼，疾張華如讎。

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified, Dan inwardly harbored shame and fear, hated Zhang Hua like an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu fell he loathed Zhang Hua for having proved him wrong.

sentences.zh: 及華外鎮，威德大著，朝論當徵為尚書令。

translations.literal: When Hua garrisoned outside, might and virtue greatly showed; court discussion was about to summon him as Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Hua governed the provinces with great prestige, the court meant to recall him as secretariat director.

sentences.zh: 紞從容侍帝，論晉魏故事，因諷帝，言華不可授以重任，帝默然而止。

translations.literal: Dan at ease attending the emperor, discussed Jin and Wei old affairs, thereby hinting to the emperor, saying Hua could not be entrusted heavy duty; the emperor silent then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dan used history lessons to persuade Sima Yan not to give Zhang Hua central power, and the idea was dropped.

sentences.zh: 事具《華傳》。

translations.literal: The affair is fully in *Hua’s biography*.
translations.idiomatic: The full story appears in Zhang Hua’s biography.

sentences.zh: ，紞疾，詔以紞為散騎常侍，賜錢二十萬、床帳一具。

translations.literal: , Dan fell ill; edict made Dan Regular Cavalier Attendant, bestowed two hundred thousand cash, one set bed curtains.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, the court named him cavalier attendant and gave him two hundred thousand cash and bedding.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 二子：播、熊。

translations.literal: Two sons: Bo and Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Feng Bo and Feng Xiong.

sentences.zh: 播，大長秋。

translations.literal: Bo, grand prolonger of autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Bo became grand prolonger of autumn at court.

sentences.zh: 熊字文羆，中書郎。

translations.literal: Xiong, courtesy name Wenpi, Palace Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xiong, courtesy name Wenpi, was a palace gentleman.

sentences.zh: 紞兄恢，自有傳。

translations.literal: Dan’s elder brother Hui has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dan’s elder brother Feng Hui has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 史評==史臣曰：夫立身之道，曰仁與義。

translations.literal: Historical judgment==The historiographer says: As for the way to stand in life, we speak of benevolence and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The historian writes that the foundation of character is benevolence and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 動靜既形，悔吝斯及。

translations.literal: Once movement and stillness take form, regret and shame follow.
translations.idiomatic: Once deeds appear, regret and blame attach to them.

sentences.zh: 有莘之媵，殊《北門》之情；

translations.literal: The Shen bride’s attendant differs from the mood of *Northern Gate*;
translations.idiomatic: The Yi bride who attended Tang was not like the bitter official in the *Beimen* ode;

sentences.zh: 渭濱之叟，匪西山之節。

translations.literal: the old man by the Wei bank did not match the integrity of the Western Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: the old man by the Wei was not the hermit of the Western Hills.

sentences.zh: 湯武有以濟其功，夏殷不能譏其志。

translations.literal: Tang and Wu had means to complete their merit; Xia and Yin could not reproach their intent.
translations.idiomatic: Tang and Wu could finish their work; Xia and Shang could not fault their purpose.

sentences.zh: 王沈才經文武，早屍人爵，在魏參席上之珍，居晉為幄中之士，桐宮之謀遽泄，武闈之禍遂臻。

translations.literal: Wang Shen’s talent spanned civil and military; early he bore noble rank without true worth; in Wei he was a delicacy on the mat; in Jin a man inside the tent; the Tong Palace plot leaked at once, disaster at the Wu Gate followed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen had ability yet betrayed his lord; honored in Wei and Jin, he leaked Cao Mao’s plot and brought calamity on the house.

sentences.zh: 是知田光之口，豈燕丹之可絕；

translations.literal: Thus we know Tian Guang’s mouth—how could Prince Dan of Yan seal it;
translations.idiomatic: As with Tian Guang, a loyal mouth cannot be silenced by fear;

sentences.zh: 豫讓之形，非智氏之能變。

translations.literal: Yurang’s mutilated form was not something the Zhi clan could alter.
translations.idiomatic: nor could the Zhi clan break Yurang’s resolve by destroying his body.

sentences.zh: 動靜之際，有據蒺藜，仁義之方，求之彌遠矣。

translations.literal: Between movement and stillness lie foot-trapping thorns; the path of benevolence and righteousness grows ever harder to find.
translations.idiomatic: Between action and inaction lie hidden snares; true benevolence and right become harder to reach.

sentences.zh: 彭祖謁由捧雉，孕本貿絲，因家乏主，遂登顯秩。

translations.literal: Pengzu owed his summons to offering a pheasant; his mother’s womb came from trading silk; with no true master in the house he still rose to high rank.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun rose from a humble mother and a pheasant-offering plea, yet climbed to power without a legitimate heir’s line.

sentences.zh: 擁北州之士馬，偶東京之糜沸，自可感召諸侯，宣力王室。

translations.literal: Holding Youzhou’s soldiers and horses, meeting the eastern capital’s turmoil, he could have rallied the lords and served the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: With northern armies during Luoyang’s collapse, he could have aided the throne.

sentences.zh: 而乘間伺隙，潛圖不軌，放肆獯虜，遷播乘輿。

translations.literal: Yet he seized his chance, secretly plotted treason, unleashed the Di and Rong, and drove the imperial carriage into exile.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he intrigued, used barbarian allies, and hounded the emperor.

sentences.zh: 遂使漳滏蕭然，黎元塗地。

translations.literal: Thereby the Zhang and Fu rivers ran bare and the common people were smeared on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The heartland was stripped bare and the people ruined.

sentences.zh: 縱貪夫于藏戶，戮高士于燕垂，阻越石之內難，邀世龍之外府。

translations.literal: He set greedy men at the gate like a hidden corpse, slew a worthy on Yan’s frontier, blocked Liu Kun’s inner strife, and courted Shi Le’s outer storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: He harbored villains, murdered scholars, thwarted Liu Kun, and curried Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 惡稔毒痡，坐致焚燎，假手仇敵，方申凶獷，慶封之戮，慢罵何補哉！

translations.literal: Evil ripened to poison; he ended in the flames; the enemy’s hand fulfilled his doom—what good did Qing Feng’s curses do!
translations.idiomatic: His wickedness brought fire and death at an enemy’s hands—curses availed nothing.

sentences.zh: 公曾，慈明之孫；

translations.literal: Gongzeng was Ciming’s grandson;
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu was grandson of the revered Xun Shuang;

sentences.zh: 景倩，文若之子，踐隆堂而高視，齊逸軌而長騖。

translations.literal: Jingqian was Wenruo’s son; he trod the high hall with lifted gaze and raced along surpassing tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yi was Xun Yu’s son, lofty in station and ambition.

sentences.zh: 孝敬足以承親，周慎足以事主，刊姬公之舊典，采蕭相之遺法。

translations.literal: Filial respect was enough to serve kin; circumspection enough to serve the ruler; he carved the Duke of Zhou’s old canons and gathered the minister Xiao’s leftover laws.
translations.idiomatic: They were dutiful sons and careful ministers, codifying ritual like the Duke of Zhou and Han precedents.

sentences.zh: 然而援朱均以貳極，煽褒閻而偶震。

translations.literal: Yet they cited Zhu and Jun to unsettle the heir, fanned Bao and Yan to shake the thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they cited wicked precedents to shake the succession and stirred palace factions.

sentences.zh: 雖廢興有在，隆替靡常，稽之人事，乃二荀之力也。

translations.literal: Though rise and fall have their causes and fortune is not constant, judged by human deeds this was the work of the two Xuns.
translations.idiomatic: Their choices, not fate alone, steered the realm’s rise and fall.

sentences.zh: 至於鬥粟興謠，逾裏成詠，勖之階禍，又已甚焉。

translations.literal: As for the bushel-grain rhyme and the lane songs, the ladder of disaster Xun Xu built was worse still.
translations.idiomatic: The rhymes foretold disaster, and Xun Xu’s scheming made it worse.

sentences.zh: 馮紞外騁戚施，內窮狙詐，斃攸安賈，交勖仇張，心滔楚費，過逾晉伍。

translations.literal: Feng Dan outward played the toady, inward exhausted monkey deceit, killed You to comfort Jia, joined Xu to make Zhang an enemy—his heart outdid Chu’s Fei and surpassed Jin’s Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dan flattered, schemed, eliminated Sima You for Jia Chong, and with Xun Xu ruined Zhang Hua—villainy rivaling the worst ministers of old.

sentences.zh: 爰絲獻壽，空取慰於仁心，紞之陳說，幸收哀於迷慮，投畀之罰無聞，《青蠅》之詩不作矣。

translations.literal: When Yuan Si offered birthday wine it vainly soothed a humane heart; when Dan spoke he luckily checked a deluded mind—yet no banishment was heard and the ode *Green Flies* went unsung.
translations.idiomatic: No punishment fit his crimes; the slander of *Qing ying* never sounded for him.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：處道文林，胡貳爾心，彭祖凶孽，自貽伊戚。

translations.literal: Eulogy says: Chudao in the literary grove—why did you double your heart? Pengzu, violent spawn, brought grief on yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Verse: Wang Shen the scholar betrayed his lord; Wang Jun the brute reaped sorrow.

sentences.zh: 臨淮翼翼，孝形於色。

translations.literal: Linhuai, cautious and careful, filial feeling showed in his face.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yi of Linhuai was reverent and filial.

sentences.zh: 安陽英英，匪懈其職。

translations.literal: Anyang, bright and bright, did not slack from duty.
translations.idiomatic: The marquis of Anyang shone in office without slacking.

sentences.zh: 傾齊附魯，是為蝥賊。

translations.literal: Overturning Qi and clinging to Lu—this is the mantis-bandit.
translations.idiomatic: Betraying kin for faction makes a pest of the state.

sentences.zh: 紞之不臧，交亂罔極。

translations.literal: Dan’s ill ways mingled chaos without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dan’s evil knew no bound.
